translation_en:
…people constantly tend from sincerity toward artifice, objects from simplicity toward ornament, rites from simplicity toward complexity, and customs from generosity toward meanness. This is not true only of recent times: even the Zhou differed in these respects from the ages of Tang Yao and Yu Shun. Such, indeed, is the tendency of things. Where circumstances inevitably tend, government must erect safeguards. Thus the sage constantly reverses artifice to restore sincerity, restrains ornament to recover simplicity, reduces complexity to achieve simplicity, and draws people away from meanness toward generosity. His practice is to diminish these excesses, never to augment them. Even when he makes additions, his intention is still to reduce them. Hence the people readily follow, and there need be no proliferation of offices. It is not that he is unwilling to establish them; there is simply no use for such excrescences.

Later generations failed to understand this intention. They used artifice to govern artifice, ornament to govern ornament, complexity to govern complexity, and meanness to govern meanness, until all under Heaven fell into confusion. Rather than seeking a return to the root, they multiplied offices to keep things going. They sought thereby to amass wealth, but wealth was depleted still further; to strengthen the troops, but the troops became still more exhausted; to suppress wrongdoing, but wrongdoing proliferated; to put punishments in order, but punishments became still more excessive. The more urgently they sought good government, the farther they departed from it. Why? Because officials’ deliberations were confused and disrupted one another.

Someone carrying a heavy load fears that the axle will break, so he piles shafts and axles on top as spares, unaware that their added weight hastens the axle’s breaking. Someone wearing a notched jade ring fears that it will break, so he wears two as a precaution, unaware that the two rings will strike each other and break all the sooner. Thus multiplying administrative business leads to multiplying offices, and multiplying offices further increases administrative business: each aggravates the harm caused by the other. title: 嘉靖三十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
事則其源也誠欲省官莫若省事其理明
甚而陳彭年乃謂省事不如省官不亦左
乎此不必論也我
朝建官斟酌今古密不以煩疎不以漏誠宜
世守而不可損益者也然承平久而虛文
盛加設則亦有矣
皇上中興悉皆罷去又汰郡邑吏數百人官少
民安事無不舉公私饒樂海內晏清久矣
頃緣事棘有司復議加設然政無恒格則
===
===
難以圖成人無恒居則爲慮不熟況徼幸
之路啓於前苟免之心持於後於是不顧
國家事體不恤百姓怨咨止務希合以規進
取而事之僨者多矣賴
主上神聖旋
詔罷之往又申
勅所司毋復增擾淵哉
聖心真明見萬里高出尋常萬萬者也顧
上務减官而下不務减事則革於今者未必不

事則其源也。誠欲省官，莫若省事，其理明甚，而陳彭年乃謂省事不如省官，不亦左乎？此不必論也。
我朝建官，斟酌今古，密不以煩，疎不以漏，誠宜世守而不可損益者也。然承平久而虛文盛，加設則亦有矣。皇上中興，悉皆罷去，又汰郡邑吏數百人，官少民安，事無不舉，公私饒樂，海內晏清久矣。頃緣事棘，有司復議加設。然政無恒格，則難以圖成；人無恒居，則爲慮不熟。況徼幸之路啓於前，苟免之心持於後，於是不顧國家事體，不恤百姓怨咨，止務希合以規進取，而事之僨者多矣。賴主上神聖，旋詔罷之，往又申勅所司，毋復增擾。淵哉！聖心真明見萬里，高出尋常萬萬者也。顧上務减官，而下不務减事，則革於今者未必不
translation_en:
…affairs are the root of it. If one truly wishes to reduce official posts, nothing is better than reducing administrative business. The principle is perfectly clear, yet Chen Pengnian asserted that reducing business was inferior to reducing posts. Was this not mistaken? There is no need to debate this.
In establishing official posts, our dynasty weighed ancient and contemporary practice: its arrangements were comprehensive without being cumbersome, and spare without leaving gaps. They truly deserve to be preserved for generations, without addition or subtraction. Yet prolonged peace brought a proliferation of empty formalities, and additional posts were indeed established. In restoring the dynasty’s flourishing rule, His Majesty abolished all these and further dismissed several hundred officials in prefectures and counties. With fewer officials, the people were at peace, and no business went unattended. Public and private alike enjoyed abundance and contentment, and all within the seas long remained tranquil.
Recently, because affairs had become pressing, the responsible authorities again proposed additional posts. Yet when administration has no stable framework, it is difficult to bring plans to completion; when men have no settled tenure, their deliberations lack maturity. Moreover, with opportunities for advancement by luck opening before them and the desire merely to escape blame driving them from behind, they disregard the proper conduct of state affairs and pay no heed to the people’s grievances. They strive only to please their superiors and secure advancement, and much business consequently comes to grief. Fortunately, our sovereign, in his divine sagacity, promptly decreed the abolition of these posts. Previously [?], he had also reiterated his command to the responsible offices not to impose further vexations. How profound is the imperial mind! Truly, its clear vision extends ten thousand li, surpassing ordinary understanding ten thousand times over. Yet while those above strive to reduce official posts, those below do not strive to reduce administrative business. Thus, what is abolished today may yet …

title: 嘉靖三十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
復於後汰於此者未必不添於彼何也官
與事相儷者也不可以獨省也且天下之
事本無若是多也惟不當而無實是故多
焉何以明其然也今夫醫之治病察虛實
辨陰陽得其所以病者而投之藥故可隨
試而輒效若不知所病而百藥雜施倖一
物之或中則醫不勝勞而病愈不可治今
也舍易於近圖艱於遠非利濟之宜也時
合而疑時去而赴非應機之筭也萬全之
===
利以小礙而廢百世之患以小便而行非
權物之度也胡然而行旋復議罷胡然而
罷又復議行非經遠之規也則無乃爲百
藥雜試者歟是故曰無當也童子相與戲
也以塵爲飯以塗爲羹以木爲胾然至日
晚必歸饟者塵飯塗羹可爲戲而不可以
食也今也鉤校簿牒往復支離非軫瘼之
切也藻績文物務爲容美非靖共之忱也
虛增聲數邀求官賞非明試之真也廋惡

translation_en:
…be restored later, and what is eliminated here may well be added there. Why? Offices and administrative business go together; one cannot reduce either alone. Moreover, the affairs of the realm were never so numerous in themselves. They multiply because undertakings are ill-judged and lack substance. How can this be demonstrated? When a physician treats illness, he examines deficiency and excess, distinguishes yin and yang, identifies the cause of the illness, and administers medicine accordingly. Thus each treatment can promptly take effect. If he does not understand the illness but indiscriminately administers a hundred medicines, hoping that one might happen to work, his labors will be endless and the illness increasingly beyond cure. Today, to abandon easy measures close at hand and pursue difficult ones far away is no fitting way to benefit and aid the people. To hesitate when the time is right and rush forward when the moment has passed is no strategy for responding to opportunity. To discard an undertaking offering assured benefit because of a minor impediment, or adopt one bringing harm for a hundred generations because of a small convenience, is no proper measure for weighing affairs. To put something into effect for no clear reason, then promptly discuss abolishing it, and to abolish something for no clear reason, then again discuss implementing it, is no plan for the long term. Is this not like trying a hundred medicines indiscriminately? This is why I call such undertakings ill-judged.
When children play together, they use dust as rice, mud as soup, and wood as slices of meat. Yet at evening they invariably return home to eat, because dust-rice and mud-soup serve for play but cannot be eaten. Today, checking and cross-checking registers and documents through endless, disjointed exchanges does not constitute earnest concern for the people's suffering. Embellishing achievements and ceremonial forms [?], striving for a beautiful outward appearance, does not constitute sincere, dutiful service. Falsely inflating claims of renown and numerical results to seek official advancement and rewards does not constitute the substance of genuine assessment through service. Concealing wrongdoing…

text:
容奸掇求曲細非詰慝之要也則無乃爲
塵飯塗羹者歟是故曰無實也夫事當則
一可以當百不當則百不可以當一實則
一爲而一成不實則百爲而百不成徒使
文例叢興姦蠹浩積而莫可繩檢乃於是
糜沸紛挐顛頓倉皇以爲可以救弊而不
知弊之所起寔乃由之非徒無益而又害
焉者也此則百年積習淪胥至斯非一朝
一夕之故者及今不亟反之恐日甚一日

有不可勝救者矣夫能必貴當則釋法爲
竒非吾能也計必貴當則參驗不合非吾
計也利必貴當則失得不償非吾利也法
必貴當則朝四暮三非吾法也兹國是所
由定也言必責實則捷給爲佞者不可飾
言也行必責實則儇利任術者不可飾行
也功必責實則比周爲譽者不可飾功也
罪必責實則巧文曲避者不可飾罪也兹
人心所由一也國是定人心一則上下之

由定也言必責實則捷給爲佞者不可飾
言也行必責實則儇利任術者不可飾行
也功必責實則比周爲譽者不可飾功也
罪必責實則巧文曲避者不可飾罪也茲
人心所由一也國是定人心一則上下之
punctuated:
容奸，掇求曲細，非詰慝之要也，則無乃爲塵飯塗羹者歟？是故曰無實也。夫事當，則一可以當百；不當，則百不可以當一。實，則一爲而一成；不實，則百爲而百不成。徒使文例叢興，姦蠹浩積，而莫可繩檢。乃於是糜沸紛挐，顛頓倉皇，以爲可以救弊，而不知弊之所起寔乃由之，非徒無益而又害焉者也。此則百年積習，淪胥至斯，非一朝一夕之故者。及今不亟反之，恐日甚一日，有不可勝救者矣。
夫能必貴當，則釋法爲竒，非吾能也；計必貴當，則參驗不合，非吾計也；利必貴當，則失得不償，非吾利也；法必貴當，則朝四暮三，非吾法也。兹國是所由定也。言必責實，則捷給爲佞者不可飾言也；行必責實，則儇利任術者不可飾行也；功必責實，則比周爲譽者不可飾功也；罪必責實，則巧文曲避者不可飾罪也。兹人心所由一也。國是定，人心一，則上下之
translation_en:
…harboring wrongdoers and picking over trifling details is not the essential way to investigate wickedness. Is this not like making rice from dust and soup from mud? Thus I call it lacking in substance. When an undertaking is appropriate, one can serve for a hundred; when inappropriate, a hundred cannot serve for one. With substance, each undertaking achieves its result; without substance, a hundred undertakings yield a hundred failures. This merely causes documentary precedents to proliferate and abuses and corruption to accumulate unchecked. Then, amid turmoil like boiling gruel, confusion, stumbling, and panic, people believe they can remedy abuses, unaware that these very practices are actually their source. They are not merely useless but positively harmful. A century of accumulated habits has brought us to this collective decline; its causes did not arise overnight. Unless we urgently reverse course now, I fear matters will worsen day by day until they can no longer be remedied.
If ability must be valued for its appropriateness, then setting aside the law to perform extraordinary feats is no ability we should recognize. If plans must be valued for their appropriateness, then a plan that fails when checked against the evidence is no plan we should adopt. If benefits must be valued for their appropriateness, then gains that do not compensate for losses are no benefits we should seek. If regulations must be valued for their appropriateness, then giving four in the morning and three in the evening—merely rearranging the same allotment—is no regulation we should adopt. In this way the guiding policy of the state is settled. If words must be held to account for their substance, glib flatterers cannot embellish their speech. If conduct must be held to account for its substance, the clever and cunning who rely on stratagems cannot embellish their conduct. If achievements must be held to account for their substance, those who form cliques to win praise cannot embellish their achievements. If offenses must be judged by the facts, those who manipulate wording and resort to devious evasions cannot disguise their offenses. In this way people’s hearts are united. When the guiding policy of the state is settled and people’s hearts are united, then between those above and those below…

title: 嘉靖三十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
間崇本尚質急當務而不為無益撓者息
躁者靜天下自可以省事事省則財用寡
財用寡則賦稅薄賦稅薄則民逸民逸則
中外靖謐風俗醇美易簡之化洽而綜核
之治成當是時也即官不必備可也多無
為可也歲有廢損焉亦可也故額定員且
或病其為多矣又何增設之足云嗟乎絲
之棼也使人理其一累千不足誠得其緒
則一人而已矣夫經綸之事固若斯焉矣
===

同考試官教諭劉 批 養士國家之先務而表
樹効用由上培之其實尤先於自養此作激昂振勵足興多
士嚮往之心宜錄以式

之道條答詳盡而識見出羣文采爛發子盖豪傑之士也宜
錄以式

間，崇本尚質，急當務而不為無益，撓者息，躁者靜，天下自可以省事。事省則財用寡，財用寡則賦稅薄，賦稅薄則民逸，民逸則中外靖謐，風俗醇美，易簡之化洽而綜核之治成。當是時也，即官不必備可也，多無為可也，歲有廢損焉亦可也。故額定員，且或病其為多矣，又何增設之足云！嗟乎！絲之棼也，使人理其一，累千不足；誠得其緒，則一人而已矣。夫經綸之事，固若斯焉矣。

第三問

同考試官教諭劉批：養士，國家之先務，而表樹効用，由上培之，其實尤先於自養。此作激昂振勵，足興多士嚮往之心，宜錄以式。

同考試官學正孫批：古人養士之典與士自養之道，條答詳盡，而識見出羣，文采爛發。子盖豪傑之士也，宜錄以式。

同考試官進士邢批：養士所以待用，則士之乗
translation_en:
…among those above and below, they will esteem fundamentals and prize substance, give priority to pressing tasks, and undertake nothing unprofitable. Those who cause disturbance will desist, and the impetuous will become calm. Affairs throughout the realm can naturally be simplified. With fewer affairs, expenditures will diminish; with diminished expenditures, taxes will be light; with light taxes, the people will enjoy ease. When the people enjoy ease, peace will prevail within and beyond the capital, and customs will become pure and good. The transforming influence of ease and simplicity will spread everywhere, and government through comprehensive scrutiny will be achieved. At such a time, it would be acceptable even to leave some official posts unfilled, to refrain from much activity, and to make abolitions and reductions each year. Even the established quota of officials might then be considered excessive; what need would there be to speak of adding posts? Alas! When silk is tangled, if each person is made to sort out one strand, even a thousand people will not suffice. But if someone truly finds the guiding thread, one person alone is enough. The work of ordering the realm is indeed like this.

Third Question

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor: Nurturing scholars is a foremost task of the state. Their distinction and useful service depend upon cultivation from above, but in truth their cultivation of themselves comes still earlier. This composition is stirring and invigorating, sufficient to awaken aspirations among the many scholars. It should be recorded as a model.

Comment by Associate Examiner Sun, School Director: The responses concerning the ancient institutions for nurturing scholars and the way scholars should cultivate themselves are detailed and exhaustive, point by point. The insight surpasses that of others, and the literary brilliance shines forth. You are surely a scholar of outstanding gifts. This should be recorded as a model.

title: 嘉靖三十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
時嚮用者當知自勵矣推究極古今發明詳盡宜錄之以
作士風
考試官侍讀高批士係所養而尤係所自養
誠為確論然非有志者不能道故特取之
考試官學士董批能知士習之敝而歷陳之他
日見用當不負所養矣
執事慨然慕古者得士之盛思養士用士
之法以振末世之習非愚所及愚學為士
者也敢為執事誦所聞焉夫古所謂養士
===
者非以其足廩餼贍俯仰而已也所以謹
化原重教本優柔涵育以成性者也古所
謂用士者非以其積資序慎繩墨而已也
所以考行誼稽實德翕受敷施以致治者
也自昔唐虞之際其法未備然設米廩之
學遵成均之舊契則敷教夔則典樂亦可
識其大矣當時九官之徒輔弼于上八才
子之輩佐佑于下詢四岳闢四門俊乂在
官明哲就列眾賢畢用其亦養之有道歟

punctuated:
時嚮用者，當知自勵矣。推究極古今，發明詳盡，宜錄之以作士風。

考試官侍讀高批：士係所養，而尤係所自養，誠為確論。然非有志者不能道，故特取之。

考試官學士董批：能知士習之敝而歷陳之，他日見用，當不負所養矣。

執事慨然慕古者得士之盛，思養士用士之法，以振末世之習，非愚所及。愚學為士者也，敢為執事誦所聞焉。夫古所謂養士者，非以其足廩餼、贍俯仰而已也，所以謹化原、重教本、優柔涵育以成性者也。古所謂用士者，非以其積資序、慎繩墨而已也，所以考行誼、稽實德、翕受敷施以致治者也。自昔唐虞之際，其法未備，然設米廩之學，遵成均之舊，契則敷教，夔則典樂，亦可識其大矣。當時九官之徒輔弼于上，八才子之輩佐佑于下，詢四岳，闢四門，俊乂在官，明哲就列，眾賢畢用，其亦養之有道歟？
translation_en:
…those who meet their opportunity and look toward service should know to exert themselves. Its inquiry ranges fully across past and present [?], and its exposition is thorough. It should be recorded to invigorate the ethos of scholars.

Comment by Examiner Gao, Reader-in-waiting: Scholars depend on how they are nurtured, and still more on how they nurture themselves. This is indeed a sound judgment. Yet only someone with resolve could express it; hence I have selected this essay in particular.

Comment by Examiner Dong, Academician: He recognizes the faults in scholars’ habits and sets them out one by one. When employed in the future, he should prove worthy of the nurturing he has received.

You, sir, earnestly admire the ancients’ abundance of worthy men and ponder their methods of nurturing and employing scholars, seeking thereby to reform the habits of this declining age. Such concerns lie beyond my humble capacity. I am one who studies to become a scholar, and venture to recount for you what I have heard. What the ancients called nurturing scholars did not consist merely in providing ample grain allowances and supporting their households. It was a means of attending carefully to the source of moral transformation, giving weight to the foundations of instruction, and gently fostering and nourishing their innate nature to its fulfillment. What the ancients called employing scholars did not consist merely in accumulating seniority and scrupulously observing rules. It was a means of examining conduct and propriety, investigating genuine virtue, broadly receiving worthy men and putting their abilities to use, so as to achieve good government.

Long ago, in the age of Tang and Yu, these methods were not yet fully developed. Nevertheless, they established the Milin school and followed the old practices of the Chengjun school. Xie spread instruction, while Kui directed music: from these things one can discern the broad outlines. At that time, the nine officials assisted the ruler above, while groups such as the eight talented men lent support below. The Four Marchmounts were consulted, and the four gates were opened. Men of outstanding ability held office, and the wise and discerning took their places in the ranks. All the worthy were employed. Was this not also because there was a proper way of nurturing them?

title: 嘉靖三十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
夏商相仍于今爲烈而其制獨詳于周孔
子稱周監二代又曰唐虞于斯爲盛蓋美
二帝而尊周也然周制所以爲善者以其
慎于所用而先于所養其先于所養者以
其得所爲教也是故內則並建四學虞庠
夏序商校三面環峙而周學居中命曰辟
雝外則四學錯置鄉立虞庠州立夏序黨
立商校而周學立侯國命曰泮宫是無地
而非教也師氏教以三德保氏教以六藝
===
司樂教以六善學正教以四術大司徒總
其十二教而又聯其師聯其友以爲教太
宰又以九兩之政繫民而教之是無官師
而非教也春秋教以禮樂冬夏教以詩書
皮弁祭菜以教之敬入學鼓篋以教之孫
射以教之德羽籥以教之秄喜則教之歌
勞則教之舞是無物而非教也入則教之
于家出則教之于族鄉則教之讀法邑則
教之懸象不于庠序則于州黨是無所往

punctuated: 夏商相仍，于今爲烈，而其制獨詳于周。孔子稱「周監二代」，又曰「唐虞于斯爲盛」，蓋美二帝而尊周也。然周制所以爲善者，以其慎于所用而先于所養；其先于所養者，以其得所爲教也。是故內則並建四學，虞庠、夏序、商校三面環峙，而周學居中，命曰辟雝；外則四學錯置，鄉立虞庠，州立夏序，黨立商校，而周學立侯國，命曰泮宫。是無地而非教也。師氏教以三德，保氏教以六藝，司樂教以六善，學正教以四術，大司徒總其十二教，而又聯其師、聯其友以爲教，太宰又以九兩之政繫民而教之。是無官師而非教也。春秋教以禮樂，冬夏教以詩書；皮弁祭菜，以教之敬；入學鼓篋，以教之孫；射以教之德，羽籥以教之秄，喜則教之歌，勞則教之舞。是無物而非教也。入則教之于家，出則教之于族；鄉則教之讀法，邑則教之懸象；不于庠序，則于州黨。是無所往
translation_en:
The Xia and Shang continued this practice in succession, and it has flourished down to the present; yet its institutions were elaborated most fully under the Zhou. Confucius declared, “The Zhou looked to the two preceding dynasties,” and also said, “Compared with Tang and Yu, this age was more flourishing.” He thus praised the two emperors while honoring the Zhou. The excellence of Zhou institutions lay in taking care over whom they employed and giving priority to nurturing them. Their nurturing came first because they understood how to educate.

Thus, within the royal capital, they established four schools together. The Yu xiang, Xia xu, and Shang xiao stood around three sides, while the Zhou school occupied the center and was called the Biyong. Outside the capital, the four kinds of school were distributed among different locations: the Yu xiang was established in townships, the Xia xu in districts, and the Shang xiao in neighborhoods; the Zhou school was established in the feudal states and called the Pangong. Thus there was no place without education.

The Preceptor taught the three virtues; the Guardian taught the six arts; the Director of Music taught the six excellences; and the School Instructor taught the four disciplines. The Minister of Education supervised the twelve teachings and further joined teachers and friends into associations for instruction. The Grand Steward also bound the people together and instructed them through the administration of the nine bonds. Thus there was no official or teacher who did not educate.

In spring and autumn they taught rites and music; in winter and summer they taught the Odes and Documents. Wearing leather caps and offering vegetables in sacrifice taught reverence. Upon entering school, opening their book boxes at the drumbeat taught humility. Archery taught virtue; dances with feathers and flutes taught zi [?]. In joy they taught singing; in toil they taught dancing. Thus there was nothing that did not serve to educate.

At home they were taught within the household; outside it, within the clan. In the townships they were taught through readings of the laws; in settlements, through publicly displayed representations of the laws. If instruction was not in the schools, it was in the districts and neighborhoods. Thus there was nowhere one could go…

title: 嘉靖三十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
而非教也而其大端則約之禮義歸之人
倫反之本心達之性命不見異物不遷他
岐優柔以俟其得從容以待其化所以養
之如此則士安得而不善乎及其用之也
比年入學中年考校七年視其小成九年
視其大成大胥頒次其所學而辨異之諸
子合諸射以考其藝而進退之其謹之庠
序者至也閭胥書其孝弟睦婣黨正書其
德行道藝州長考其德行道藝而勸之鄉
===

之鄉者至也鄉大夫論其秀者升之司徒

論其秀者升之司馬曰進士其升之朝者

punctuated: 而非教也。而其大端，則約之禮義，歸之人倫，反之本心，達之性命，不見異物，不遷他岐，優柔以俟其得，從容以待其化。所以養之如此，則士安得而不善乎？及其用之也，比年入學，中年考校，七年視其小成，九年視其大成。大胥頒次其所學而辨異之，諸子合諸射以考其藝而進退之，其謹之庠序者至也。閭胥書其孝弟睦婣，黨正書其德行道藝，州長考其德行道藝而勸之，鄉老、鄉大夫帥其吏與其衆寡而賓之，其選之鄉者至也。鄉大夫論其秀者，升之司徒，曰選士；司徒論其秀者，升之國學，曰俊士；國學論其秀者而免其征，曰造士；大樂正論其秀者，升之司馬，曰進士。其升之朝者至也。升之司馬者，掌之司士而詔王官之；列之官者，掌之太宰而詔王廢置之。以德詔爵，以功詔祿，以能詔事，以乆奠食，其用之位者至也。而其大端，則考其行之所成
translation_en:
…wherever one went, there was instruction. Its principal aims were to discipline them through ritual propriety and righteousness, direct them toward the human relationships, restore them to their original minds, and bring them to an understanding of their nature and Heaven’s mandate. They were not exposed to distracting things or diverted onto other paths. They were nurtured gently while awaiting their understanding, and given time while awaiting their transformation. With such means of nurturing them, how could scholars fail to become good?

When it came to employing them, students entered school every year and were assessed every other year. In the seventh year their lesser attainment was examined; in the ninth, their greater attainment. The Senior Music Instructor (daxu) assigned them ranks according to what they had learned and distinguished their accomplishments. The Director of Noble Sons (zhuzi) assembled them for archery to assess their skills and advance or demote them. The care exercised over them in the schools was thus thoroughgoing. The Neighborhood Head recorded their filial devotion, fraternal respect, and harmony with their kin and relatives by marriage. The Community Head recorded their virtuous conduct and accomplishments in the Way and the arts. The District Chief examined these qualities and encouraged them. The Township Elders and Township Grand Masters led their subordinate officials and the assembled populace in honoring them as guests. Their selection within the townships was thus thoroughgoing.

The Township Grand Master assessed the outstanding men and advanced them to the Minister of Education, calling them “selected scholars” (xuanshi). The Minister of Education assessed the outstanding men among them and advanced them to the state school, calling them “eminent scholars” (junshi). The state school assessed its outstanding men and exempted them from service obligations, calling them “accomplished scholars” (zaoshi). The Director of Music assessed the outstanding men among them and advanced them to the Minister of War, calling them “advanced scholars” (jinshi). Their advancement to court was thus thoroughgoing. Those advanced to the Minister of War came under the Director of Personnel, who advised the king on appointing them to office. Those placed in the ranks of officialdom came under the Grand Steward, who advised the king on their dismissal or retention. Rank was recommended according to virtue, emoluments according to achievement, and duties according to ability; their provision was fixed according to length of service. Their employment in official positions was thus thoroughgoing. Its principal aim was to examine what they had achieved in their conduct…

title: 嘉靖三十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
校其學之所得飾于學者不能欺于鄉矯
于鄉者不能隱于學其用之安得而不實
乎愚觀周制未嘗不廢書而嘆焉曰嗟乎
士生于周其非下愚而至于弗率教者未
之有矣其非甚不肖而至于弗慎其官者
未之有矣譬之農夫之于禾播之以時耨
之以節防其旱潦驅其螟螣日至而穀弗
登者吾固弗信也譬之慈母之于赤子襁
而護之携而鞠之防其燠寒適其食飲年
===
至而赤子弗得其長者吾固弗信也是以
下得其養而上得其用人才之多莫有過
于周者而治化之極亦莫有加于周者紀
冊是載詩人美之自文王開基而首務飭
學一時皆彬彬而興其詩曰肆成人有德
小子有造譽髦斯士及武王營鎬京而國
學攸始不言其戰伐之功而以天下之服
歸之于學其詩曰鎬京辟雍無思不服皇
王烝哉當是時追稱文王之德以及賢士

王烝哉當是時追稱文王之德以及賢士
punctuated:
校其學之所得。飾于學者不能欺于鄉，矯于鄉者不能隱于學，其用之安得而不實乎？
愚觀周制，未嘗不廢書而嘆焉，曰：「嗟乎！士生于周，其非下愚而至于弗率教者，未之有矣；其非甚不肖而至于弗慎其官者，未之有矣。譬之農夫之于禾，播之以時，耨之以節，防其旱潦，驅其螟螣，日至而穀弗登者，吾固弗信也。譬之慈母之于赤子，襁而護之，携而鞠之，防其燠寒，適其食飲，年至而赤子弗得其長者，吾固弗信也。」是以下得其養，而上得其用。人才之多，莫有過于周者，而治化之極，亦莫有加于周者。紀冊是載，詩人美之。
自文王開基，而首務飭學，一時皆彬彬而興。其詩曰：「肆成人有德，小子有造，譽髦斯士。」及武王營鎬京，而國學攸始，不言其戰伐之功，而以天下之服歸之于學。其詩曰：「鎬京辟雍，無思不服，皇王烝哉！」當是時，追稱文王之德，以及賢士
translation_en:
…and assess what they have gained through learning. Those who put on a show at school cannot deceive their home communities; those who dissemble in their home communities cannot conceal themselves at school. How, then, could their employment in office fail to rest on genuine merit?
Whenever I contemplate the institutions of the Zhou, I cannot help laying aside my book and sighing: “Alas! Among scholars born under the Zhou, none but the most incurably foolish could have failed to follow its instruction; none but the most unworthy could have failed to attend conscientiously to their offices. Consider a farmer tending his grain: he sows at the proper time, weeds at the proper intervals, guards against drought and flooding, and drives off the grain pests. That the harvest season should arrive without the grain ripening—I simply cannot believe it. Consider a loving mother tending her infant: she swaddles and protects it, carries and nurtures it, shields it from heat and cold, and provides suitable food and drink. That the years should pass without the infant growing—I simply cannot believe it.” Thus those below received their nurturing, while those above secured their service. No age surpassed the Zhou in its abundance of talented men, and none exceeded it in the perfection of its government and moral transformation. The historical records attest to this, and the poets praise it.
From the time King Wen laid the foundations of the dynasty, his foremost concern was to put education in order, and men of cultivated character arose throughout his age. The poem says: “Thus the adults possessed virtue, and the young had attainments—renowned and outstanding were these men.” When King Wu built Haojing, the state school was established there. Rather than speaking of his achievements in warfare, the poem attributes the submission of All Under Heaven to education. It says: “At Haojing’s Biyong school, none thought of withholding submission. How great was the august king!” At that time, they retrospectively praised King Wen’s virtue, extending their praise also to worthy scholars…

title: 嘉靖三十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
其詩曰思皇多士維周之楨又追武王桓
桓之功而士亦附之以成顯績其詩曰保
有厥士于以四方盖周之功不獨一人之
烈而已士實相乗而起以並効于時其詩
曰疏附先後奔走禦侮然士之所以足貴
者以其有本也其詩曰有馮有翼有孝有
德至于後世而仁義陵遲學校不作青衿
刺焉士或在野進用失宜候人作焉及周
之旣衰諸侯分列而所以維持其闕匡救
===
其危者賢士往往猶秉周禮雖强大國皆
詘而服焉夫其翼戴襄賛以致其理者如
彼其隆也彌縫調護以保其後者又如是
其切也是以年過其歷名垂于今孔子所
稱盛者不有然歟自是而後分爭于戰國
大壞于秦至漢武帝始表章六經置太學
設博士弟子員人人質問其意亦厚矣開
賢良文學孝廉諸科招致天下一藝悉赴
郡邑待詔公車其法亦周矣故遺經畢出

punctuated:
其詩曰：「思皇多士，維周之楨。」又追武王桓桓之功，而士亦附之，以成顯績。其詩曰：「保有厥士，于以四方。」盖周之功，不獨一人之烈而已，士實相乗而起，以並効于時。其詩曰：「疏附先後，奔走禦侮。」然士之所以足貴者，以其有本也。其詩曰：「有馮有翼，有孝有德。」至于後世，而仁義陵遲，學校不作，《青衿》刺焉；士或在野，進用失宜，《候人》作焉。及周之旣衰，諸侯分列，而所以維持其闕、匡救其危者，賢士往往猶秉周禮，雖强大國，皆詘而服焉。夫其翼戴襄賛，以致其理者，如彼其隆也；彌縫調護，以保其後者，又如是其切也。是以年過其歷，名垂于今。孔子所稱盛者，不有然歟？
自是而後，分爭于戰國，大壞于秦。至漢武帝，始表章六經，置太學，設博士弟子員，人人質問，其意亦厚矣。開賢良、文學、孝廉諸科，招致天下一藝，悉赴郡邑，待詔公車，其法亦周矣。故遺經畢出
translation_en:
…The ode says: “Admirable are the many worthy men: they are the pillars of Zhou.” It also recalls King Wu’s martial achievements, in which worthy men joined him to accomplish illustrious deeds. The ode says: “He retained his worthy men, and through them possessed the four quarters.” Zhou’s achievements were surely not the exploits of one man alone. Worthy men arose in succession, together rendering service in their age. The ode says: “They drew the distant near, attached the people to him, guided and supported him, hastened in his service, and resisted aggression.” Yet what made these men worthy of esteem was that they had a firm foundation. The ode says: “There were those who gave support and assistance, those who possessed filial devotion and virtue.” In later generations, benevolence and righteousness declined, and schools ceased to flourish; “Green Collars” (Qingjin) criticized this. Worthy men were sometimes left outside office, and appointments were improperly made; “The Officer Awaiting Guests” (Houren) was composed in response. Once Zhou had declined and the regional lords stood divided, those who made good its deficiencies and rescued it from peril were worthy men who still upheld Zhou ritual. Even powerful states yielded and submitted to them. So great was their support and assistance in bringing about its good government; so earnest, too, were their efforts to repair breaches and provide careful protection, preserving it for later generations. Thus its years exceeded its allotted span, and its fame endures to this day. Was this not why Confucius praised its flourishing abundance of talent?
Thereafter came division and contention in the Warring States period, and great ruin under Qin. Only with Emperor Wu of Han were the Six Classics first brought to prominence, the National University established, and student places under the Erudites instituted, so that everyone could ask questions and seek clarification. His intentions were indeed generous. He opened the various recruitment categories for the Worthy and Good, Literary Learning, and Filial and Incorrupt, attracting men throughout the realm who possessed even a single skill. They all proceeded to the commanderies and counties and awaited imperial summons at the Office of Public Carriages. His arrangements were indeed comprehensive. Thus all the surviving classics came to light…

title: 嘉靖三十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
羣才並用自漢以賢良文學名者仲舒以
下凡十七人孝廉鮑宣以下凡二十三人
而試吏如路温舒以下二十二人以貲爲
郎者張釋之司馬相如二人漢之得人亦
復稱盛皆自武帝起之也然先王之化必
本于教漢之教道既寡而興賢雖多亦所
謂齊其末者也所得者號皆當世之才而
往往多雜較之古遠矣然其人皆重質務
實貴樸賤華忠信之道未薄而躬行之誼
===
尚存亦有可覽觀者漢又數詔羣吏趣其
選舉不舉孝者以不敬論不察廉者以不
勝任論亦得多方收攬之意焉固近古之
徵也後世益復去古學宫未甞不設而養
士之道漸微矣諸科未甞不廣而用士之
道漸失矣夫考德問業所以辨志而傅之
咕嗶繁之文詞此誦習之陋也况師儒既
懈則弁其誦習者而益舛之求士能養不
可得也鄉舉里選所以察賢而沿之資格

道漸失矣夫考德問業所以辨志而傳之

懈則并其誦習者而益外之求士能養不

punctuated:
羣才並用。自漢以賢良文學名者，仲舒以下凡十七人；孝廉，鮑宣以下凡二十三人；而試吏，如路温舒以下二十二人；以貲爲郎者，張釋之、司馬相如二人。漢之得人亦復稱盛，皆自武帝起之也。然先王之化必本于教，漢之教道既寡，而興賢雖多，亦所謂齊其末者也。所得者號皆當世之才，而往往多雜，較之古遠矣。然其人皆重質務實，貴樸賤華，忠信之道未薄，而躬行之誼尚存，亦有可覽觀者。漢又數詔羣吏趣其選舉，不舉孝者以不敬論，不察廉者以不勝任論，亦得多方收攬之意焉，固近古之徵也。
後世益復去古，學宫未甞不設，而養士之道漸微矣；諸科未甞不廣，而用士之道漸失矣。夫考德問業，所以辨志，而傅之咕嗶繁之文詞，此誦習之陋也。况師儒既懈，則弁其誦習者而益舛之，求士能養不可得也。鄉舉里選，所以察賢，而沿之資格
translation_en:
…and men of many talents were employed together. Among those who became known under the Han through the categories of Worthy and Good and Literary Learning, there were seventeen in all, beginning with Zhongshu; through Filial and Incorrupt, twenty-three in all, beginning with Bao Xuan; and among probationary officials, twenty-two, including Lu Wenshu and those after him. Two became Gentlemen through their wealth: Zhang Shizhi and Sima Xiangru. The Han, too, was celebrated for obtaining talented men, and all this began with Emperor Wu. Yet the transforming influence of the former kings necessarily rested upon education. Under the Han, provision for education was scant; although many worthy men were advanced, this was still what is called attending only to the outward results. Those recruited were reputed to be the talents of their age, but their quality was often mixed, falling far short of antiquity. Nevertheless, they valued substance and practical conduct, esteemed simplicity and disdained ornament. The way of loyalty and trustworthiness had not yet grown weak, and the commitment to putting principles into personal practice still survived. There was thus something worth considering in their example. The Han also repeatedly issued edicts urging officials to proceed with selection and recommendation. Failure to recommend the filial was judged disrespectful; failure to identify the incorrupt was judged incompetence in office. This, too, embodied the intention of drawing in talent by many means, and was certainly evidence of an affinity with antiquity.
Later ages departed still further from antiquity. Schools continued to be established, yet the way of nurturing scholars gradually declined. The categories of recruitment remained extensive, yet the way of employing scholars was gradually lost. Examining virtue and inquiring into studies were intended to distinguish aspirations, but these practices became attached to prolix literary compositions [?]: this was the failing of rote recitation and study. Moreover, once the teachers themselves grew negligent, even that recitation and study became increasingly distorted [?], so that one could no longer hope for scholars to be properly nurtured. Recommendation from the districts and selection from the villages were intended to discern the worthy, but came to follow formal qualifications …

title: 嘉靖三十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
循之品第此拘常之見也而况官守不專
則并其拘常者而復奪之求士能用不可
得也然則人性本同而所繫于時者則異
故曰古之成才也易後之成才也難夫成
才而易則中人有可勉者及當其難則特
立自拔者功亦半焉此其勢然也嘉穀莫
藝雖榮弗實矣赤子離保雖趨弗達矣自
漢以後士之不能自振者夫亦有所由也
明興斟酌百王悉準周禮古之遺法湮滅千
===
載者一旦而舉之至我
皇上尤復加念深
詔有司興禮文崇
化道天下更始自新若闢
乾坤而揭日月矣于此時而不知所勵焉無乃
甚失其會者乎夫俗習者世之所沿也士
者所以更俗者也愚觀近日士習凡數變
矣盖弘治之前士皆相守以愿相核以實
不務矯矯之名赫赫之行爲吏者以無害

…and follow classifications of rank: this is the outlook of those bound by convention. Worse still, when officials do not attend exclusively to their duties, even that adherence to convention is taken away. One then cannot obtain scholars fit for employment. Human nature is fundamentally the same, but the conditions imposed by the times differ. Thus it is said: in antiquity it was easy to develop talent; in later ages it became difficult. When developing talent is easy, even people of middling ability can be encouraged to achieve it. When it becomes difficult, even those who stand independently and rise above their fellows achieve only half as much. This follows from the circumstances themselves. If fine grain is left uncultivated, it may flourish but will not bear fruit; if an infant is separated from its nurse, it may hasten forward but will not reach its destination. Since the Han, there have likewise been reasons why scholars have been unable to raise themselves up.
When the Ming arose, it weighed the practices of the kings of successive ages and took the Rites of Zhou as its standard throughout. Surviving institutions of antiquity that had lain buried for a thousand years were restored at a stroke. Our present Emperor has given the matter still greater attention, earnestly commanding the responsible officials to promote ritual observances and exalt the way of moral transformation. All under Heaven have made a fresh beginning and renewed themselves, as though Heaven and Earth had been opened anew and the sun and moon raised aloft. 為能論治者以無動為大循日月報期會
厪厪引繩墨不敢失尺寸焉雖靡過舉然
欲以策時趨事弗能矣乃或起而飭之好
氣喜俠務以警動一世作文章尚節槩多
譏評往往弗得其中顧亦有足奇者天下
翕然從焉然文不可勝氣不可激今遂因
而懲之懲之誠是也玆愚觀士之為習則

They followed the calendar and submitted reports by the appointed deadlines, scrupulously adhering to established rules, not daring to deviate by an inch. Although they committed no errors in their conduct, they could not devise responses to the times or attend energetically to affairs. Then some arose to rouse and discipline them. They prized spirit and admired chivalry, striving to startle and awaken an entire age. They composed writings, esteemed integrity, and frequently offered critical judgments. …when distorted, they restore them to balance; when customs are base, they urge people to exert themselves; when customs favor advancement, they restrain it; when customs favor withdrawal, they draw people forward. Present customs outwardly display baseness and weakness, while inwardly people pursue their desire for advancement. In my humble view, selecting men who remain steadfast and unchanging is the means to remedy weakness; selecting men of lofty conduct and unsullied integrity is the means to remedy baseness; and selecting men who live contentedly in retirement and obscurity among mountains and forests is the means to restrain the pursuit of advancement. Thus the sage king’s correction of customs proceeds like a revolving cycle, and customs change imperceptibly, simply because he holds the controlling handle and regulates when to restrain and when to release. In employing scholars, he thus embodies the principle of nurturing them. Nothing could be better than this. Moreover, with the supreme sage upon the throne, the moment his thought turns to this matter, transformation will sweep through like wind and thunder: lesser effects scarcely merit mention.
Nevertheless, the initiative in nurturing and employing scholars rests with those above, while cultivating oneself and awaiting employment is one’s own responsibility. What Mengzi calls “rousing oneself” is the genuine intention to do good and the essential nature of the heart. One’s goodness should not arise because of others, nor should one’s wrongdoing cease because of others. 自警者也。狂瞽之言，不知執事以爲何如？

第四問

同考試官教諭吳批：天人之理甚微，而人皆以其意爲說，徒用滋惑，理學所以不明也。此策闡發箕疇，獨窺實際，不襲舊聞，言確義精，超脫直截，可定古今未决之疑，知其所得深矣。錄之以爲窮理者法。

同考試官教諭李批：洪範庶徵，箕子以理言之則明，漢儒以迹求之則鑿，遂使衆論紛紜，迄今莫定。子獨出真見，不蹈常言，反覆辨論，委曲詳盡，令人豁然有悟，非深究天人之蘊者不能爲也。定是佳士，健羨健羨！

考試官侍讀高批：天人之際，論者甚多，然皆不得其理，文談而已。此作似有實見，故特表出之。

考試官學士董批：漢以後談天人者愈多，傅會其說愈支，京房、翼奉之流，學者所以弗道也。此作明暢通達，特寫胸臆，良是佳士。
translation_en:
…to admonish myself. These rash and benighted words—I do not know what you, sir, will think of them.

Fourth Question

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, School Instructor: The principles governing Heaven and humanity are exceedingly subtle, yet people all explain them according to their own notions, merely multiplying confusion. This is why the learning of principle remains obscure. This policy essay elucidates the categories expounded by Jizi, uniquely discerning their true substance without repeating received accounts. Its statements are sound and its meaning precise; it rises above conventional views and goes straight to the point. It can resolve doubts left unsettled from antiquity to the present. We can see how profound the author's understanding is. It is included here as a model for those who investigate principle.

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, School Instructor: As for the various manifestations in the Great Plan, Jizi explained them in terms of principle and thus made them clear; Han Confucians sought their meaning in outward signs and thus forced their interpretations. Consequently, conflicting opinions proliferated, and no resolution has been reached even now. You alone offer genuine insight without following conventional statements. You examine and debate the matter repeatedly, treating its intricacies thoroughly and in detail, bringing the reader to sudden understanding. Only someone who has deeply investigated the mysteries of Heaven and humanity could accomplish this. You are certainly a fine scholar. How greatly I admire you, how greatly I admire you!

Comment by Examiner Gao, Hanlin Reader-in-Waiting: Very many have discussed the relationship between Heaven and humanity, yet none have grasped its principles; theirs is merely literary talk. This composition seems to contain genuine insight, so I have singled it out for recognition.

Comment by Examiner Dong, Hanlin Academician: Since the Han, those discussing Heaven and humanity have grown ever more numerous, and their strained explanations have become increasingly ramified. This is why scholars do not speak of the likes of Jing Fang and Yi Feng. This composition is lucid, fluent, and penetrating, directly expressing the author's own thoughts. He is indeed a fine scholar.

title: 嘉靖三十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
夫天人之際豈不至微眇難言者哉然在
天有實理在人有實事而曲說不與焉何
謂實理夫陰陽錯行乖和貞勝鬱而為沴
雖天不能以自主此實理也何謂實事夫
防其未生救其既形備飭慮周勝以人勝
此實事也至謂天以某災應某事是誣天
也謂人以某事致某災是誣人也皆求其
理而不得曲為之說者也君子奚取之哉
嗟乎非達天人之故通虛而不滯者何足
===
以語此而愚非其人也然執事既有問焉
則又胡可以無對夫古之言天者曰天垂
象見吉凶而已未始推所為也言事天者
曰克謹天戒而已未始著所招也乃如庶
徵之說詳於洪範其休徵曰肅時雨若乂
時暘若哲時燠若謀時寒若聖時風若其
咎徵曰狂恒雨若僭恒暘若豫恒燠若急
恒寒若蒙恒風若言感通之靡忒也若曰
天人一理即呼吸動靜皆有所關而不可

punctuated:
夫天人之際，豈不至微眇難言者哉？然在天有實理，在人有實事，而曲說不與焉。何謂實理？夫陰陽錯行，乖和貞勝，鬱而為沴，雖天不能以自主，此實理也。何謂實事？夫防其未生，救其既形，備飭慮周，勝以人勝，此實事也。至謂天以某災應某事，是誣天也；謂人以某事致某災，是誣人也。皆求其理而不得，曲為之說者也。君子奚取之哉？

嗟乎！非達天人之故、通虛而不滯者，何足以語此？而愚非其人也。然執事既有問焉，則又胡可以無對？夫古之言天者曰：「天垂象，見吉凶。」而已，未始推所為也。言事天者曰：「克謹天戒。」而已，未始著所招也。乃如庶徵之說，詳於《洪範》。其休徵曰：「肅，時雨若；乂，時暘若；哲，時燠若；謀，時寒若；聖，時風若。」其咎徵曰：「狂，恒雨若；僭，恒暘若；豫，恒燠若；急，恒寒若；蒙，恒風若。」言感通之靡忒也。若曰天人一理，即呼吸動靜皆有所關，而不可
translation_en:
Is not the relationship between Heaven and humanity supremely subtle and difficult to discuss? Yet Heaven has actual principles, and human affairs have practical tasks; strained explanations have no place in either. What are actual principles? Yin and yang operate in interweaving courses; discord and harmony continually alternate in predominance. When their forces become pent up, they produce baleful influences. Even Heaven cannot control this at will. These are actual principles. What are practical tasks? Prevent calamities before they arise and remedy them once they take shape; make preparations thorough and deliberations comprehensive, and overcome them through human effort. These are practical tasks. To say that Heaven responds to a particular affair with a particular calamity is to misrepresent Heaven; to say that people bring about a particular calamity through a particular action is to misrepresent humanity. Such claims are all strained explanations devised by those who have sought the underlying principles but failed to grasp them. Why should a gentleman accept them?

Alas! Unless one understands the workings of Heaven and humanity and has an open, unobstructed understanding, how could one adequately discuss this? I am not such a person. Yet since you, honored sir, have posed the question, how could I leave it unanswered? Those in antiquity who spoke of Heaven merely said, “Heaven displays images, revealing good and ill fortune”; they never sought to infer what occasioned them. Those who spoke of serving Heaven merely said, “Be duly attentive to Heaven’s warnings”; they never specified what had called them forth. Now the account of the various signs is set out in detail in the “Great Plan” chapter of the Book of Documents. Of auspicious signs it says: “Reverence: timely rain follows; good governance: timely sunshine follows; discernment: timely warmth follows; deliberation: timely cold follows; sagacity: timely wind follows.” Of adverse signs it says: “Wild misconduct: incessant rain follows; overstepping: incessant sunshine follows; indolence: incessant warmth follows; haste: incessant cold follows; benightedness: incessant wind follows.” This speaks of the unfailing character of mutual influence and response. It is as if to say that Heaven and humanity share one principle: even breathing, movement, and stillness all have a bearing upon it, and one cannot…

title: 嘉靖三十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
不謹云耳君子以是求之得其意焉可也
如其辭而已矣則貌何以爲雨言何以爲
暘視何以爲燠聽何以爲寒思何以爲風
矧時雨必有時暘是肅則不必乂也時燠
必有時寒是晢則不必謀也而恒暘必無
恒雨是有僭應則無狂應也恒寒必無恒
燠是有急應則無豫應也初豈若是膠固
矣乎其曰王省惟歲卿士惟月師尹惟日
言修弭之當豫也若曰君臣一體即大小
===
不同而莫不當謹云耳君子亦以是求之
得其意焉可也如其辭而已矣則王何分
於歲卿士何分於月師尹何分於日矧王
省惟歲則月在其中卿士可無省也卿士
惟月則日在其中師尹可無省也而積日
爲月則師尹之省亦卿士也積月爲歲則
卿士之省亦王也初豈若是局滯矣乎至
哉孔子之春秋也書災異不書事應說者
謂其恐有不合反以啓人之不信此又得

translation_en:
…must therefore be treated with care—that is all. The gentleman may approach it in this way and grasp its meaning. If one merely follows its wording, however, why should demeanor produce rain, speech sunshine, sight warmth, hearing cold, and thought wind? Moreover, timely rain must coexist with timely sunshine: would this mean that reverence need not entail good order? Timely warmth must coexist with timely cold: would this mean that discernment [?] need not entail deliberation? Conversely, constant sunshine necessarily excludes constant rain: would a response to presumption therefore exclude a response to recklessness? Constant cold necessarily excludes constant warmth: would a response to impetuosity therefore exclude a response to indolence? Could the original meaning possibly have been so rigid?
When it says, “The king examines the year; the high ministers, the month; the various officials, the day,” it means that corrective measures to avert calamity should be taken in advance. It is as if to say that ruler and ministers form one body: although their responsibilities differ in magnitude, all must exercise care—that is all. Here too, the gentleman may approach it in this way and grasp its meaning. If one merely follows its wording, however, why should the king be assigned the year, the high ministers the month, and the various officials the day? Moreover, if the king examines the year, the months are included within it, and the high ministers could dispense with examination. If the high ministers examine the month, the days are included within it, and the various officials could dispense with examination. Conversely, days accumulate into months, so the examination undertaken by the various officials would also be that of the high ministers; months accumulate into years, so the examination undertaken by the high ministers would also be that of the king. Could the original meaning possibly have been so restrictive?
How consummate is Confucius’s Spring and Autumn Annals! It records calamities and anomalies but does not record the human affairs to which they supposedly responded. Commentators say that he feared that some correspondences might fail to hold, thereby provoking disbelief instead. This, too, is to grasp …

title: 嘉靖三十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
其似未得其真者也夫聖人之宅心也至
公而其據理也至正如其理即不合而不
為之拘如非其理即合而不為之泥彼災
異之不可以事應言也乃其理自如此聖
人蓋灼見而實言之非故有意隱約乎其
間也如必符之以箕範則書大雨者必求
何事之狂書大旱者必求何事之僭書無
氷者必求何事之豫書隕霜殺菽者必求
何事之急書六鷁退飛者必求何事之蒙
===
===
而可乎災於一歲是謂何王災於一月謂
何卿士災於一日謂何師尹而可乎故愚
以為論災異者必當以春秋為準其意真
其辭直確乎不易者也而於箕範則取其
意不以辭害焉可也甚矣天人之際未易
言也謂和致祥固也然以堯之聖乃有洪
水以湯之聖乃有暵旱何其舛也而楚莊
無災至禱於神魯宣大有至書諸史又何
順也豈莊宣之德有加於堯湯者乎謂誠

translation_en:
…its semblance, without grasping its truth. The sage’s disposition is utterly impartial, and his reliance on principle utterly correct. If something accords with principle, he is not constrained by its failure to match events; if it does not accord with principle, he is not bound by it even when it does match. That calamities and anomalies cannot be explained as responses to particular affairs follows from principle itself. The sage clearly perceived this and spoke of it truthfully; he did not deliberately conceal or obscure anything in his words. If one insists on making these records tally with Jizi’s Great Plan, then whenever heavy rain is recorded, one must seek the act of unruliness responsible; whenever severe drought is recorded, the act of overstepping; whenever an absence of ice is recorded, the act of laxity; whenever frost falling and killing the beans is recorded, the act of severity; and whenever six yi waterbirds flying backward are recorded, the act of benightedness. Can this be acceptable? If a calamity occurs in a particular year, which king does it implicate? If in a particular month, which minister? If on a particular day, which official? Can this be acceptable?

Thus, in my humble view, those who discuss calamities and anomalies must take the Spring and Autumn Annals as their standard. Its meaning is true, its language straightforward: it stands firmly beyond alteration. As for Jizi’s Great Plan, one may grasp its meaning without letting its wording impair that meaning.

How very difficult it is to speak of the relations between Heaven and humanity! To say that harmony brings auspicious signs is certainly sound. Yet despite Yao’s sageliness, there was the great flood; despite Tang’s sageliness, there was scorching drought. How contrary things were! Yet King Zhuang of Chu suffered no calamities, to the point that he prayed to the spirits about it; and Duke Xuan of Lu enjoyed a great harvest, to the point that it was recorded in the annals. How favorable things were for them! Could the virtue of Zhuang and Xuan have surpassed that of Yao and Tang? To say that sincerity…

title: 嘉靖三十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
動天固也然堯必九年始免於水湯必七
年始免於旱何其遲也而大戊修德祥桑
即枯宋景善言熒惑即退又何速也豈戊
景之誠有加於堯湯者乎蓋天地之間惟
一氣而已矣氣之行也有時而順有時而
舛而其復也有時而速有時而遲時乎舛
也雖堯湯不能禦其来猶之時乎順也則
莊宣可以安享者也不然可謂舛不為堯
湯而順獨為莊宣乎復而遲也雖堯湯不
===
能驅之去猶之復而速也則戊景可以坐
值者也不然可謂遲不為堯湯而速獨為
戊景乎此其理自有在可以深思而黙會
者也柰何談者之紛紛也彼謂不足畏而
漫然者無足言也乃必究其所從来則亦
非也蓋天有天之道而人有人之為易之
洊雷震而恐懼修省也乃君子之心不容
自已焉者猶孔子迅雷烈風而變也詩之
敬天怒渝而無敢戲豫馳驅也則亦所謂

punctuated: 動天，固也。然堯必九年始免於水，湯必七年始免於旱，何其遲也！而大戊修德，祥桑即枯；宋景善言，熒惑即退，又何速也！豈戊、景之誠有加於堯、湯者乎？蓋天地之間，惟一氣而已矣。氣之行也，有時而順，有時而舛；而其復也，有時而速，有時而遲。時乎舛也，雖堯、湯不能禦其来，猶之時乎順也，則莊、宣可以安享者也。不然，可謂舛不為堯、湯而順獨為莊、宣乎？復而遲也，雖堯、湯不能驅之去，猶之復而速也，則戊、景可以坐值者也。不然，可謂遲不為堯、湯而速獨為戊、景乎？此其理自有在，可以深思而黙會者也。柰何談者之紛紛也！彼謂不足畏而漫然者，無足言也；乃必究其所從来，則亦非也。蓋天有天之道，而人有人之為。《易》之「洊雷，震」，而恐懼修省也，乃君子之心不容自已焉者，猶孔子迅雷烈風而變也。《詩》之敬天怒渝，而無敢戲豫馳驅也，則亦所謂
translation_en:
…moves Heaven: this is certainly so. Yet Yao had to wait nine years before being freed from the flood, and Tang seven years before being freed from drought. How slow this was! Yet when Taiwu cultivated virtue, the portentous mulberry immediately withered; when Duke Jing of Song spoke good words, Mars immediately withdrew. How swift this was! Could the sincerity of Taiwu and Duke Jing have surpassed that of Yao and Tang?

Between Heaven and Earth there is only a single vital force, qi. Its movement is sometimes harmonious and sometimes contrary; its return to normal is sometimes swift and sometimes slow. When conditions are contrary, even Yao and Tang cannot prevent their arrival, just as, when conditions are harmonious, King Zhuang of Chu and Duke Xuan of Lu can enjoy them in peace. Otherwise, can we say that adverse conditions were not brought about for Yao and Tang, while favorable conditions were brought about expressly for King Zhuang and Duke Xuan? When recovery is slow, even Yao and Tang cannot drive the adversity away, just as, when recovery is swift, Taiwu and Duke Jing may encounter it without doing anything. Otherwise, can we say that slowness was not intended for Yao and Tang, while swiftness was intended expressly for Taiwu and Duke Jing? There is an underlying principle here, which one can grasp silently through deep reflection. Why, then, all this contentious talk?

Those who say that these things need not be feared and remain indifferent are not worth discussing. Yet to insist on investigating precisely what brought them about is also mistaken. Heaven has its own Way, and human beings have their own sphere of action. The Book of Changes says, “Repeated thunder: Zhen.” To respond with fear, self-cultivation, and self-examination is something the noble man’s heart cannot help doing—just as Confucius changed his demeanor at sudden thunder and violent winds. The Book of Odes enjoins reverence for Heaven’s anger and its changes, daring neither to indulge in play and pleasure nor to dash about recklessly. This, too, is what is meant by…

title: 嘉靖三十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
恐懼修省者也此皆人事當然不可不盡
堯之所謂儆予湯之所以禱於桑林固此
意也至夫災之所以然則天道運行微乎
微者矣而豈夫人可能測識者哉矧天之
大德曰生乃使愆厲流行民物凋瘁斯豈
天心所忍爲乎蓋亦有無如之何者也而
今必曰有意爲之則天其無乃不好生歟
此愚所謂誣也自斯義之不明故乃有稱
乾封餘烈如公孫卿公孫弘之流者焉乃有
===

其意於此而貢諛者則求其意於彼雖其
意有媺惡然皆不得其故君子所不道也
執事云其理雖微必有一定之說而欲愚
虛思以對夫既畧言之矣請遂爲之畢其
義夫天之災猶夫人之病也病必有徵其
血脉乖錯徵於色而發於聲皆元氣之不
足爲之也其病不一乃雜出而互見焉者

恐懼修省者也。此皆人事當然，不可不盡。堯之所謂儆予，湯之所以禱於桑林，固此意也。至夫災之所以然，則天道運行微乎微者矣，而豈夫人可能測識者哉？矧天之大德曰生，乃使愆厲流行，民物凋瘁，斯豈天心所忍爲乎？蓋亦有無如之何者也。而今必曰有意爲之，則天其無乃不好生歟？此愚所謂誣也。自斯義之不明，故乃有稱乾封餘烈，如公孫卿、公孫弘之流者焉；乃有旁摭曲證，牽附無當，如京房、翼奉之流者焉。蓋惟必謂天爲有意，是故陳規者則求其意於此，而貢諛者則求其意於彼。雖其意有媺惡，然皆不得其故，君子所不道也。
執事云：「其理雖微，必有一定之說。」而欲愚虛思以對。夫既畧言之矣，請遂爲之畢其義。夫天之災，猶夫人之病也。病必有徵，其血脉乖錯，徵於色而發於聲，皆元氣之不足爲之也。其病不一，乃雜出而互見焉者
translation_en:
…these too are instances of fear, self-cultivation, and self-examination. All these are proper human duties, which must be fulfilled completely. This was surely the meaning of Yao’s words, “Admonish me,” and of Tang’s prayer at Sanglin. As for why disasters occur, however, the workings of the Way of Heaven are subtle beyond subtlety. How could anyone fathom and understand them? Moreover, Heaven’s great virtue is called life-giving. Could Heaven bear to let calamities spread and people and other living things wither away? Surely there are also things about which nothing can be done. Yet if one now insists that Heaven does these things intentionally, would that not mean that Heaven takes no delight in life? This is what I humbly call misrepresentation. Because this principle has not been understood, there have been people like Gongsun Qing and Gongsun Hong who praised the lingering potency of qianfeng [?]; and people like Jing Fang and Yi Feng who gathered miscellaneous evidence, distorted it into proofs, and forced connections that did not fit. Precisely because they insist that Heaven acts intentionally, those offering admonition seek its intention in one direction, while those offering flattery seek it in another. Although their motives differ in goodness and wickedness, none of them grasps the underlying cause. Such claims are not things a gentleman would voice.
You say, “Although the principle is subtle, there must be a definitive explanation,” and wish me to ponder it with an open mind and reply. Having already spoken of it briefly, let me now complete the explanation. Disasters in Heaven are like illnesses in a person. Illness necessarily has signs: disorder in the blood and vessels shows itself in the complexion and manifests itself in the voice. All this is caused by an insufficiency of primal qi. The illnesses are various, appearing in combination and manifesting themselves by turns…

title: 嘉靖三十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
非謂以手足之病致耳目之病以耳目之
病致腹心之病也災亦有徵在天則見於
象緯在地則見於山川在物則為鳥獸草
木之妖在人則為奸宄寇賊之戾皆元氣
之不足為之也其災不一亦雜出而互見
焉者非謂以人之變致物之變以人物之
變致天地之變也夫災而至於有徵則氣
之方舛可知其所底止既難以窺而復之
遲速又難以度可畏孰甚焉於是修人事
===
以勝之庶乎有不為害不然乃亦不至於
太甚而可從容以需其復苟遂不為之所
則有不可者矣是故謹疾者必為之求醫
藥寡嗜慾節飲食慎起居以固一身之元
氣謹災者必為之修紀綱審法令懲欺罔
黜殘虐省刑罰薄稅斂蠲逋負廣儲蓄賑
貧窮收攜貳除盜賊慎邊防以固國家之
元氣凡皆盡其在我者以俟之而已迨其
氣之既復陂者平否者泰而吾亦無所損

氣之既復陂者平否者泰而吾亦無所損
punctuated: 非謂以手足之病致耳目之病，以耳目之病致腹心之病也。災亦有徵：在天則見於象緯，在地則見於山川，在物則為鳥獸草木之妖，在人則為奸宄寇賊之戾，皆元氣之不足為之也。其災不一，亦雜出而互見焉者，非謂以人之變致物之變，以人物之變致天地之變也。夫災而至於有徵，則氣之方舛可知。其所底止既難以窺，而復之遲速又難以度，可畏孰甚焉？於是修人事以勝之，庶乎有不為害；不然，乃亦不至於太甚，而可從容以需其復。苟遂不為之所，則有不可者矣。是故謹疾者必為之求醫藥，寡嗜慾，節飲食，慎起居，以固一身之元氣；謹災者必為之修紀綱，審法令，懲欺罔，黜殘虐，省刑罰，薄稅斂，蠲逋負，廣儲蓄，賑貧窮，收攜貳，除盜賊，慎邊防，以固國家之元氣。凡皆盡其在我者以俟之而已。迨其氣之既復，陂者平，否者泰，而吾亦無所損
translation_en:
…This does not mean that an illness of the hands and feet causes an illness of the ears and eyes, or that an illness of the ears and eyes causes an illness of the abdomen and heart. Disasters likewise have signs: in heaven they appear in celestial configurations; on earth they appear in mountains and rivers; among other living things they take the form of anomalies in birds, beasts, grasses, and trees; among human beings they take the form of the violence of malefactors, raiders, and bandits. All are brought about by a deficiency of primal vital energy. These disasters are diverse, arising in various combinations and appearing together. This does not mean that disturbances among human beings cause disturbances among other living things, or that disturbances among human beings and other living things cause disturbances in heaven and earth.

When disasters reach the point of displaying signs, we can know that vital energy is becoming disordered. It is difficult to discern where this will end, and equally difficult to gauge how slowly or quickly recovery will come. What could be more alarming? We therefore put human affairs in order to overcome these disasters, hoping that they may cause no harm. Failing that, at least the harm may not become too severe, and we may calmly await recovery. Simply to make no provision for them would be unacceptable.

Thus, those who take illness seriously must seek physicians and medicines, curb their appetites and desires, regulate their food and drink, and take care in their daily routines, thereby strengthening the primal vital energy of the body. Those who take disasters seriously must put the governing order in good repair, scrutinize laws and ordinances, punish deception, dismiss the cruel and oppressive, reduce punishments, lighten taxation, remit arrears, enlarge reserves, relieve the poor, win back those whose allegiance is wavering, eliminate bandits, and attend carefully to frontier defense, thereby strengthening the primal vital energy of the state. All this amounts simply to doing everything within our power while awaiting recovery. Once that vital energy has recovered, what was uneven becomes level, obstruction gives way to flourishing, and we ourselves suffer no loss…

title: 嘉靖三十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
失敗壞於其間則以有備無患理之固然
者耳猶之寒暑者天也而吾為之裘為之
葛裘葛誠具則寒暑不侵焉備在我也不
曰吾有裘葛而天遂不吾寒暑也然而寒
暑有時遷也猶之風雨者天也而吾為之
室為之盖室盖誠具則風雨不侵焉備在
我也非曰吾有室盖而天遂不吾風雨也
然而風雨有時止也故善論治者不計災
與不災但視備與弗備昔堯之水也平水
===
土教稼穡其備素具是故水以九年而黎
民之雍自若也湯之旱也修六事舉荒政
其備素具是故旱以七年而兆民之殖自
若也彼楚莊即無災固未可語於堯湯之
治也而況於魯宣乎大戊即退災之速固
未必加於堯湯九年七年之間也而況於
宋景乎然則堯湯以其災愈於人之不災
以其退災之遲愈於人之不遲則夫必巳
而不必乎天之說也是故聖人之事天也

室爲之蓋室蓋誠具則風雨不侵焉備在
我也非曰吾有室蓋而天遂不吾風雨也
然而風雨有時止也故善論治者不計災
與不災但視備與弗備昔堯之水也平水
===

未必加於堯湯九年七年之間也而況於

以其退災之遲愈於人之不遲則夫必已
而不必乎天之說也是故聖人之事天也
punctuated: 失敗壞於其間，則以有備無患，理之固然者耳。猶之寒暑者，天也，而吾為之裘，為之葛。裘葛誠具，則寒暑不侵焉，備在我也。不曰吾有裘葛，而天遂不吾寒暑也。然而寒暑有時遷也。猶之風雨者，天也，而吾為之室，為之盖。室盖誠具，則風雨不侵焉，備在我也。非曰吾有室盖，而天遂不吾風雨也。然而風雨有時止也。故善論治者，不計災與不災，但視備與弗備。昔堯之水也，平水土，教稼穡，其備素具，是故水以九年，而黎民之雍自若也。湯之旱也，修六事，舉荒政，其備素具，是故旱以七年，而兆民之殖自若也。彼楚莊即無災，固未可語於堯湯之治也，而況於魯宣乎？大戊即退災之速，固未必加於堯湯九年七年之間也，而況於宋景乎？然則堯湯以其災愈於人之不災，以其退災之遲愈於人之不遲，則夫必巳而不必乎天之說也。是故聖人之事天也，
translation_en:
…loss or ruin in the meantime: this is simply because preparedness averts calamity, as reason necessarily dictates. Cold and heat, for example, come from Heaven, yet we provide ourselves with fur robes and garments of hemp. Once these are fully supplied, cold and heat cannot assail us: preparedness rests with us. This does not mean that, because we possess fur robes and hemp garments, Heaven will no longer subject us to cold and heat. Yet cold and heat change in their season. Wind and rain likewise come from Heaven, yet we provide ourselves with rooms and roofs. Once these are fully supplied, wind and rain cannot assail us: preparedness rests with us. This does not mean that, because we possess rooms and roofs, Heaven will no longer subject us to wind and rain. Yet wind and rain cease in their time. Thus those who discuss good government well do not reckon whether disasters occur, but look only to whether preparations have been made.

During the flood in Yao’s time, waterways and land were put in order, and the people were taught to sow and reap. Preparations were fully in place; hence, although the flood lasted nine years, the common people remained harmonious as before. During Tang’s drought, he attended to the six matters and implemented famine relief measures. Preparations were fully in place; hence, although the drought lasted seven years, the multitude continued to thrive as before. Even had King Zhuang of Chu suffered no disaster, his government could certainly not be spoken of alongside that of Yao and Tang—how much less that of Duke Xuan of Lu! Even though Taiwu’s disaster receded swiftly, he did not necessarily surpass Yao and Tang during their nine and seven years of calamity—how much less Duke Jing of Song! Thus Yao and Tang, despite their disasters, surpassed others who had none; despite the slow recession of their disasters, they surpassed others whose disasters receded without delay. This illustrates the principle of demanding what is required of oneself rather than making demands upon Heaven [?]. Therefore, in the sage’s service to Heaven…

title: 嘉靖三十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
純乎敬而已非因無災而弛有災而始致
也惟其所太過不及者則爲之財成輔相
焉也其於民也純乎仁而已非因無災而
輟有災而始加也惟其所憾於天地者則
爲之補助焉也處常處變事有不同然而
人者盡天且賴之固不能以終違也茲所
謂實者也達乎是則所謂惟聖時憲惟臣
欽若者可得其意焉則所謂上下勤恤以
受天永命者可得其意焉而以論於天人
===
之際其庶矣乎不然而徒訿訿爲議迄無
指歸則豈惟有𥡴於春秋之旨亦非洪範
之意所以示人者矣執事試虛聽焉定以
爲然否
第五問
同考試官教諭楊 批 自古禦戎上策莫有
過于內治者唐虞三代之隆率由茲道是策深明內
安爲外攘之本且考証古今商確事宜皆究極本末

同考試官教諭楊　批　自古禦戎上策莫有
過于内治者唐虞三代之隆率由茲道是策深明内
安爲外攘之本且考証古今商確事宜皆究極本末
punctuated:
純乎敬而已，非因無災而弛、有災而始致也。惟其所太過不及者，則爲之財成輔相焉也。其於民也，純乎仁而已，非因無災而輟、有災而始加也。惟其所憾於天地者，則爲之補助焉也。處常處變，事有不同，然而人者盡，天且賴之，固不能以終違也。茲所謂實者也。達乎是，則所謂「惟聖時憲，惟臣欽若」者，可得其意焉；則所謂「上下勤恤，以受天永命」者，可得其意焉。而以論於天人之際，其庶矣乎！不然而徒訿訿爲議，迄無指歸，則豈惟有𥡴於春秋之旨，亦非洪範之意所以示人者矣。執事試虛聽焉，定以爲然否？

第五問

同考試官教諭楊批：自古禦戎上策，莫有過于內治者。唐虞三代之隆，率由茲道。是策深明內安爲外攘之本，且考証古今，商確事宜，皆究極本末。
translation_en:
…consists solely in reverence. It is not relaxed because there are no disasters, nor first brought fully to bear when disasters occur. Only where there is excess or deficiency does the sage regulate and assist the workings of Heaven. His dealings with the people likewise consist solely in benevolence. This does not cease because there are no disasters, nor begin to be extended only when disasters occur. Only where Heaven and Earth leave the people wanting does he provide supplementation and assistance. Dealing with ordinary circumstances and responding to extraordinary changes involve different tasks. Yet when human responsibilities are fully discharged, Heaven itself depends upon them and surely cannot remain opposed to them forever. This is what is meant by substantive action. Once this is understood, one can grasp the meaning of the saying, “Take the sage as your model; let ministers reverently follow.” One can likewise grasp the meaning of “Those above and below diligently care for the people, thereby receiving Heaven’s enduring mandate.” To discuss the relationship between Heaven and humanity on this basis would surely come close to the truth! Otherwise, merely engaging in carping debate without ever reaching a definite conclusion would not only conflict with the purport of the Spring and Autumn Annals [?]; it would also depart from what the “Great Plan” intends to teach. May you, sir, listen with an open mind and determine whether this is correct.

Fifth Question

Comment by Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor: Since antiquity, no superior strategy for resisting the Rong has surpassed good internal government. The flourishing ages of Tang and Yu and of the Three Dynasties all followed this path. This policy essay makes thoroughly clear that internal peace is the foundation for repelling external enemies. Moreover, it examines evidence from antiquity and the present and carefully weighs appropriate measures, thoroughly investigating both fundamentals and particulars…

title: 嘉靖三十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
視之勦述陳言無裨實用者殆不同矣經濟才猷不
于此可槩見耶敬服敬服
考試官侍讀高批攘夷必先內治此培養元
氣之說可謂有深識矣得士如此良以自慶
考試官學士董批帝王重內治此不易之論
也子盖有志于世者讀其言若未盡焉爲之歛袵
夫夷狄之爲中國患久矣愚甞竊迹前事
自古有道之世未甞無夷狄者盖非夷狄
之足患而在中國治安之有其具也昔唐
===
虞之聖極矣有苗始而弗率繼而逆命自
二帝不能免于夷狄故專以蠻夷猾夏爲
憂世皆言干羽之格爲德化之盛而不知
其克艱之治政在養民得禹而九功敘天
地平得稷而百穀成烝民粒內則四岳百
僚熈績于朝外則羣后十二牧亮采于邦
國當其時民既以協和時雍謳歌里閭而
萬方咸乂矣苗雖蠢茲侮慢其能動咸乂
之民而擾協和之治乎故有苗之逆不足

視之勦述陳言、無裨實用者，殆不同矣。經濟才猷，不于此可槩見耶？敬服，敬服！

考試官侍讀高批：攘夷必先內治，此培養元氣之說，可謂有深識矣。得士如此，良以自慶。

考試官學士董批：帝王重內治，此不易之論也。子盖有志于世者，讀其言若未盡焉，爲之歛袵。

夫夷狄之爲中國患久矣。愚甞竊迹前事，自古有道之世，未甞無夷狄者。盖非夷狄之足患，而在中國治安之有其具也。昔唐虞之聖極矣，有苗始而弗率，繼而逆命。自二帝不能免于夷狄，故專以蠻夷猾夏爲憂。世皆言干羽之格爲德化之盛，而不知其克艱之治，政在養民。得禹而九功敘、天地平，得稷而百穀成、烝民粒。內則四岳百僚熈績于朝，外則羣后十二牧亮采于邦國。當其時，民既以協和時雍，謳歌里閭，而萬方咸乂矣。苗雖蠢茲侮慢，其能動咸乂之民，而擾協和之治乎？故有苗之逆不足
translation_en:
…Compared with those who merely plagiarize and repeat stale sayings of no practical use, this is altogether different. Does this not give us a fair indication of his talent and resourcefulness in statecraft? I admire it greatly, greatly!

Comment by Examiner Gao, Reader-in-waiting: To repel the barbarians, one must first put internal government in order. This argument for nurturing the state's vital energies shows profound insight. To have selected a scholar such as this is truly cause for congratulating ourselves.

Comment by Examiner Dong, Academician: Emperors and kings give priority to internal government: this is an unalterable principle. You are surely a man intent on serving the world. Reading your words, I feel that their meaning is not yet exhausted, and straighten my robes in respect.

The Yi and Di have long been a source of trouble for the Central Kingdom. I have ventured, in my humble way, to examine past events. Since antiquity, even ages governed according to the Way have never been without Yi and Di. The real concern, however, lies in whether the Central Kingdom possesses the means to secure orderly and peaceful government. In antiquity, the sagehood of the rulers of Tang and Yu—Yao and Shun—reached its highest perfection. Yet the Miao first refused to submit and subsequently defied their commands. Even these two emperors could not escape troubles with the Yi and Di, and therefore made the disruption of the Xia by the Man and Yi their particular concern. Everyone speaks of the Miao's submission through dances with shields and plumes as the supreme achievement of moral transformation, yet they do not understand that the government by which these rulers overcame difficulties lay in nourishing the people. With Yu in their service, the nine achievements were put in order, and Heaven and Earth were brought into harmony; with Ji, the grains ripened and the multitude had grain to eat. Within the court, the Four Mountains and the hundred officials gloriously fulfilled their duties; beyond it, the various lords and the twelve regional governors faithfully discharged their tasks in the states. At that time, the people already lived in concord and harmony, singing praises in their villages, and all regions enjoyed orderly government. Although the Miao stirred in insolent defiance, could they unsettle a people enjoying such universal order, or disturb a government marked by concord? Thus the Miao's defiance was insufficient to…

title: 嘉靖三十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
以損二帝之化而其既格適足以彰二帝
之隆以其治安之極也自三代以降莫盛
于周盖文武三代之聖王而宣王有周之
令主也當文王為西伯時海内未壹邗耆
混夷之屬不恭厥命稍以侵陵其勢固宜
及武王而天下歸周九夷通道八蠻底貢
然采薇出車文武之所以治外者也采薇
言靡室靡家獫狁之故則是有獫狁之侵
也出車言薄伐西戎則是有西戎之梗也
===
太公封齊萊戎爭國則是東海猶未定也
淮夷徐戎相率畔周而齊得賜履魯作盻
誓則是易世未幾而疆内多虞也至于宣
王而獫狁益棘淮徐繹騷蠻荆為讐姜戎
繼起宣乃南征北伐不遑寧居既以有定
而千畝之戰猶復敗績盖犬戎與周相為
終始矣然文武之德顯于西土式于四方
懷保永清之政民志既洽而周召之徒入
則篤棐輔佑于君成迂衡之功出則保釐

太公封齊萊戎爭國則是東海猶未定也
淮夷徐戎相率畔周而齊得賜履魯作肸
誓則是易世未幾而疆内多虞也至于宣
王而玁狁蠢棘淮徐繹騷蠻荆爲讐姜戎
繼起宣乃南征北代不遑寧居既以有定
而千畝之戰猶復敗績蓋犬戎與周相爲
終始矣然文武之德顯于西土式于四方
懷保永清之政民志既洽而周召之徒入
則篤棐輔佑于君成迓衡之功出則保釐
punctuated: 以損二帝之化，而其既格，適足以彰二帝之隆，以其治安之極也。自三代以降，莫盛于周。盖文武，三代之聖王，而宣王，有周之令主也。當文王為西伯時，海内未壹，邗耆混夷之屬不恭厥命，稍以侵陵，其勢固宜。及武王而天下歸周，九夷通道，八蠻底貢。然《采薇》《出車》，文武之所以治外者也。《采薇》言「靡室靡家，獫狁之故」，則是有獫狁之侵也。《出車》言「薄伐西戎」，則是有西戎之梗也。太公封齊，萊戎爭國，則是東海猶未定也。淮夷徐戎相率畔周，而齊得賜履，魯作《盻誓》，則是易世未幾，而疆内多虞也。至于宣王，而獫狁益棘，淮徐繹騷，蠻荆為讐，姜戎繼起。宣乃南征北伐，不遑寧居。既以有定，而千畝之戰猶復敗績。盖犬戎與周相為終始矣。然文武之德，顯于西土，式于四方；懷保永清之政，民志既洽。而周召之徒，入則篤棐輔佑于君，成迂衡之功；出則保釐
translation_en: …to diminish the transforming influence of the Two Emperors. Once the Miao submitted, this served precisely to display the Two Emperors’ greatness, for their orderly and peaceful government had reached its highest perfection. From the Three Dynasties onward, none flourished more than Zhou. Kings Wen and Wu were sage kings of the Three Dynasties, and King Xuan was an excellent ruler of Zhou. When King Wen was Earl of the West, all within the seas was not yet united. Such peoples as Han, Qi, and the Hunyi [?] failed to obey his commands respectfully and gradually made incursions; under those circumstances, this was only to be expected. By King Wu’s time, all under Heaven had given allegiance to Zhou: the Nine Yi opened routes of communication, and the Eight Man brought tribute. Yet “Gathering Vetch” (Cai wei) and “Sending Out the Chariots” (Chu che) show how Wen and Wu dealt with external peoples. “Gathering Vetch” says, “We have neither house nor home, because of the Xianyun”; thus there were invasions by the Xianyun. “Sending Out the Chariots” says, “We marched to attack the Western Rong”; thus there was obstruction by the Western Rong. When the Grand Duke was enfeoffed in Qi, the Lai Rong contested possession of the state; thus the eastern seaboard was still unsettled. The Huaiyi and Xu Rong followed one another in rebelling against Zhou, while Qi received a grant of territorial jurisdiction and Lu produced the “Oath at Bi” [?]; thus, only a short time after the change of reign, there were already many troubles within the realm. By King Xuan’s time, the Xianyun had grown still more threatening, the peoples of Huai and Xu stirred up repeated disturbances, the Man of Jing became enemies, and the Jiang Rong rose in succession. Xuan therefore campaigned south and north, with no leisure to dwell in peace. Even after some stability had been achieved, he again suffered defeat at the battle of Qianmu. Indeed, the Quanrong and Zhou were entwined from beginning to end. Yet the virtue of Wen and Wu shone in the western lands and furnished a model for the four quarters. Their government, which cherished and protected the people and secured lasting peace, had already won the people’s wholehearted allegiance. Men such as the Dukes of Zhou and Shao, when serving at court, earnestly supported and assisted their ruler, achieving the accomplishments of ministerial assistance [?]; when serving outside the court, they protected and governed…

title: 嘉靖三十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
于民著甘棠勿剪之化而當時之大夫素
絲羔羊之士皆以正直節儉共襄于時其
治遂與唐虞比隆而宣王承厲之衰側身
修行憂民慮災民是以有斯干鴻鴈之樂
而其臣以仲山甫之出納補王之衮召虎
之来宣作王之翰吉甫申甫之輩文武為
憲揉王之邦蓋亦不媿厥祖者焉是以夷
狄之侵文武不以其故貶王而宣王亦稱
中興之治未有治得而夷狄能患者也自
===
周之後王迹熄而夷狄横並爭于戰國而
苦于秦中國之未安固無可言者漢高帝
起亭長提三尺除秦滅項威震天下及海
內既定以三十萬衆而受圍白登遂用建
信之謀定和親之策當是時匈奴冒頓最
强桀敖滋甚及至文景天下大定矣乘先
世征伐之威撫一統之業而匈奴數入雲
中上郡鴈門北地烽火達于甘泉中行說
小豎耳日夜教單于苦漢尤甚漢乃卑詞

punctuated:
于民，著甘棠勿剪之化。而當時之大夫，素絲羔羊之士，皆以正直節儉共襄于時，其治遂與唐虞比隆。而宣王承厲之衰，側身修行，憂民慮災，民是以有《斯干》《鴻鴈》之樂。而其臣，以仲山甫之出納，補王之衮；召虎之来宣，作王之翰；吉甫申甫之輩，文武為憲，揉王之邦，蓋亦不媿厥祖者焉。是以夷狄之侵，文武不以其故貶王，而宣王亦稱中興之治。未有治得而夷狄能患者也。
自周之後，王迹熄而夷狄横，並爭于戰國而苦于秦，中國之未安固無可言者。漢高帝起亭長，提三尺，除秦滅項，威震天下。及海內既定，以三十萬衆而受圍白登，遂用建信之謀，定和親之策。當是時，匈奴冒頓最强，桀敖滋甚。及至文景，天下大定矣，乘先世征伐之威，撫一統之業，而匈奴數入雲中、上郡、鴈門、北地，烽火達于甘泉。中行說，小豎耳，日夜教單于，苦漢尤甚。漢乃卑詞
translation_en:
…among the people, displaying a transforming influence such that they would not cut down the sweet pear tree associated with their benefactor. The great officers of that time, men of the integrity celebrated in “Lambskins” with its white silk threads, all joined in sustaining their age through uprightness and frugality. Their government thus rivaled in splendor that of Tang and Yu. King Xuan, inheriting the decline under King Li, humbled himself and cultivated his conduct, caring for the people and taking thought for disasters. The people consequently enjoyed the happiness celebrated in “The Si Stream” (Si gan) and “Wild Geese” (Hong yan). Among his ministers, Zhong Shanfu, in conveying commands and reporting affairs, mended the king’s ceremonial robe—that is, remedied his shortcomings; Shao Hu came to spread the royal influence and served as the king’s pillar; and men such as Jifu and Shenfu took civil and martial virtue as their model and brought harmony to the king’s realm. They too did not disgrace their forebears. Thus, despite incursions by the Yi and Di, Kings Wen and Wu were not on that account deemed any less worthy as kings, while King Xuan’s government was likewise praised as a restoration. There has never been a case in which government was properly conducted yet the Yi and Di could bring calamity upon it.
After the Zhou, the ways of the true kings disappeared and the Yi and Di ran rampant. Amid the competing struggles of the Warring States and the suffering under Qin, the lack of peace in the central realm hardly needs discussion. Emperor Gao of Han rose from being a village head, took up a three-foot sword, overthrew Qin, and destroyed Xiang Yu; his might shook all under Heaven. Yet after the realm had been settled, he was surrounded at Baideng despite having an army of three hundred thousand. He therefore adopted the proposal of Jianxin [?] and settled upon a policy of peace through marriage alliances. At that time Modu of the Xiongnu was at the height of his power, and his defiance and arrogance grew ever greater. By the reigns of Emperors Wen and Jing, the realm had attained great stability. They drew upon the prestige of their predecessors’ campaigns and maintained the unified empire, yet the Xiongnu repeatedly invaded Yunzhong, Shangjun, Yanmen, and Beidi, and beacon warnings reached Ganquan. Zhonghang Yue was merely a petty fellow, but day and night he advised the chanyu, bringing particularly severe hardship upon Han. Han thereupon resorted to humble language…

title: 嘉靖三十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
以將之厚幣以結之若奉驕子視其侵邊
輒兢兢謹禦之若待遽客未嘗能有創焉
自今言之困阨莫如高帝卑詘莫如文景
然天下稱高帝之神武而頌文景之治平
不衰則以中國之安也夫高帝承秦後傷
痍者未起勞者未復務寬大除煩苛一切
與民更始易敝通變以開漢基功莫大焉
文景休養生息弛山澤發倉庾先禮義後
刑罰緩征薄賦使民樂生恭儉惇厚以成
===
漢業德莫盛焉而當時之臣以蕭相國之
收集曹平陽之守成民用不擾而文景專
意撫輯其臣一時多長者而河南守吳公
蜀守文翁治稱不嚴而民化天下慕之彼
其所以安中國之民者有此具也故漢至
元狩六年府庫貫朽而不可校大倉之粟
紅腐而不可食天下殷庶財用充足于是
大將軍青驃騎將軍去病等得以全力攻
逐匈奴城朔方築受降封狼胥絕大幕單

punctuated: 以將之，厚幣以結之，若奉驕子；視其侵邊，輒兢兢謹禦之，若待遽客，未嘗能有創焉。自今言之，困阨莫如高帝，卑詘莫如文景，然天下稱高帝之神武，而頌文景之治平不衰，則以中國之安也。夫高帝承秦後，傷痍者未起，勞者未復，務寬大，除煩苛，一切與民更始，易敝通變，以開漢基，功莫大焉。文景休養生息，弛山澤，發倉庾，先禮義，後刑罰，緩征薄賦，使民樂生，恭儉惇厚，以成漢業，德莫盛焉。而當時之臣，以蕭相國之收集、曹平陽之守成，民用不擾；而文景專意撫輯，其臣一時多長者，而河南守吳公、蜀守文翁，治稱不嚴而民化，天下慕之。彼其所以安中國之民者，有此具也。故漢至元狩六年，府庫貫朽而不可校，大倉之粟紅腐而不可食，天下殷庶，財用充足。于是大將軍青、驃騎將軍去病等，得以全力攻逐匈奴，城朔方，築受降，封狼胥，絕大幕，單
translation_en:
…to deal with them, and lavish gifts to bind them, as though indulging a spoiled child. Whenever they invaded the frontier, the Han anxiously took precautions against them, as though receiving an unexpected guest, but never managed to inflict a punishing blow upon them. Looking back from the present, none suffered greater straits than Emperor Gao, and none humbled themselves more than Emperors Wen and Jing. Yet the world has never ceased praising Emperor Gao’s divine martial prowess and extolling the peaceful government of Wen and Jing, because they brought security to the Central Realm.

Emperor Gao succeeded the Qin when those wounded had not yet recovered and those exhausted had not yet regained their strength. He devoted himself to generous government, abolished vexatious and harsh measures, and made a fresh beginning with the people in all things. By reforming worn-out institutions and adapting to changed circumstances, he laid the foundations of the Han: no achievement was greater. Wen and Jing allowed the people to rest, recuperate, and prosper. They relaxed restrictions on the mountains and marshes, opened the granaries, gave precedence to ritual propriety and righteousness over punishments, eased levies and reduced taxes, and enabled the people to take pleasure in life. Through reverence, frugality, sincerity, and generosity, they brought the Han enterprise to fruition: no virtue was more abundant.

Among the ministers of that time, Chancellor Xiao’s work of bringing things together and Cao, Marquis of Pingyang’s preservation of what had been achieved ensured that the people were not disturbed. Wen and Jing devoted themselves to comforting and uniting the people, and many of their ministers were men of mature virtue. Lord Wu, Governor of Henan, and Wen Weng, Governor of Shu, were renowned for governing without severity while transforming the people, and all the world admired them. Such were the means by which they secured the people of the Central Realm.

Thus, by the sixth year of Yuanshou, the strings holding the coins in the Han treasuries had rotted, and the money could no longer be counted; the grain in the imperial granary had reddened and decayed until it was inedible. Throughout the realm the people prospered, and financial resources were ample. Consequently, General-in-Chief Qing, General of Agile Cavalry Qubing, and others were able to devote their full strength to attacking and driving out the Xiongnu. They fortified Shuofang, built Shouxiang, performed a sacrificial rite on Mount Langxu [?], and crossed the great desert; the chanyu…

title: 嘉靖三十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
于遠北渾邪右袵而諸將軍分道各出擒
名王懸首漢闕下者不可勝數則以乗積
安之餘力固易爲功也嚮使元狩以後果
能用戰勝之力務內固之謀深念遠慮銷
萌杜微仁拊義育以功德與民民易集矣
顧將帥利戰而不反諸臣玩勝而不圖徼
一時之權而忽萬世之策遂使地拓而民
敝兵振而財詘于是大農錢不繼而楊可
告緡出矣軍興不足而咸陽孔僅等析秋
===
毫矣民抗敝以巧法而張趙刺深及反唇
矣天下蕭然盜賊起而直指出矣當是時
漢事幾有不可爲者故愚嘗以元狩之功
非盡將帥之能也中國之積安貽之也及
其蕭然非兵威之乏也所以安之者未得
其道也故中國而安則雖夷狄交横而不
足以爲虞中國而未安則雖勝軍擒虜闢
地開境而不足以爲恃故七國之興連吳

于遠北渾邪右祉而諸將軍分道各出擒
名王懸首漢闕下者不可勝數則以乘積
安之餘力固易爲功也嚮使元狩以後果
能用戰勝之力務内固之謀深念遠慮銷
萌杜微仁拊義育以功德與民民易集矣
顧將帥利戰而不反諸臣玩勝而不圖徼
一時之權而忽萬世之策遂使地拓而民
敝兵振而財詘于是大農錢不繼而楊可
告緡出矣軍興不足而咸陽孔僅等析秋
===
毫矣民抗敝以巧法而張趙刺深及反唇
矣天下蕭然盜賊起而直指出矣當是時

punctuated: 于遠北，渾邪右袵，而諸將軍分道各出，擒名王、懸首漢闕下者不可勝數，則以乗積安之餘力，固易爲功也。嚮使元狩以後，果能用戰勝之力，務內固之謀，深念遠慮，銷萌杜微，仁拊義育，以功德與民，民易集矣。顧將帥利戰而不反，諸臣玩勝而不圖，徼一時之權而忽萬世之策，遂使地拓而民敝，兵振而財詘。于是大農錢不繼，而楊可告緡出矣；軍興不足，而咸陽、孔僅等析秋毫矣；民抗敝以巧法，而張、趙刺深及反唇矣；天下蕭然，盜賊起，而直指出矣。當是時，漢事幾有不可爲者。故愚嘗以元狩之功，非盡將帥之能也，中國之積安貽之也；及其蕭然，非兵威之乏也，所以安之者未得其道也。故中國而安，則雖夷狄交横，而不足以爲虞；中國而未安，則雖勝軍擒虜，闢地開境，而不足以爲恃。故七國之興，連吳、楚、齊、趙之强，帶甲數十百萬，未能西攘尺
translation_en:
…the chanyu withdrew far to the north, and Hunye adopted robes fastening on the right, acknowledging Chinese rule. The generals advanced separately along different routes; the renowned kings they captured and whose heads they hung beneath the Han palace towers were beyond counting. Drawing on the surplus strength accumulated through prolonged peace, they naturally found success easy to achieve. Had they, after the Yuanshou era, truly used the strength gained through victory to pursue plans for securing the realm internally—thinking deeply and looking far ahead, eliminating troubles at their inception and preventing even their slightest beginnings, comforting the people with benevolence, nurturing them with righteousness, and sharing with them the benefits of their achievements and virtue—the people could readily have been brought to contentment.

Yet the commanders sought advantage in warfare without reflecting, and the ministers reveled in victory without planning ahead. They pursued momentary expedients while neglecting strategies for ten thousand generations. Thus territory expanded while the people became exhausted; military power flourished while financial resources dwindled. When the funds of the Chamberlain for the National Treasury no longer sufficed, Yang Ke’s denunciations of unreported taxable wealth appeared. When resources for military mobilization fell short, Xianyang, Kong Jin, and others began splitting hairs in their exactions. The people resisted their impoverishment by manipulating the law [?], while Zhang and Zhao pursued ever more searching prosecutions, extending even to those who talked back. The realm was desolate, bandits arose, and special investigators were dispatched.

At that time, the affairs of Han had almost become unmanageable. Thus I have always thought that the achievements of the Yuanshou era were not wholly attributable to the generals’ abilities: they were a legacy of the accumulated peace of the central realm. When desolation subsequently prevailed, it was not because military might was lacking, but because the proper means of securing peace had not been found. If the central realm is at peace, even foreign peoples running rampant on every side are insufficient cause for anxiety. If the central realm is not at peace, even defeating armies, capturing enemies, and expanding its territory and borders provide no dependable support. Thus, when the Seven Kingdoms rose in rebellion, combining the strength of Wu, Chu, Qi, and Zhao, with armored troops numbering in the hundreds of thousands or even a million, they could not seize even a foot of ground to the west…

title: 嘉靖三十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
寸駢首以就漢誅由中國安也陳豨兵精
而起代英布善陳而反楚韓王信材武而
連吳諸侯數起而天下不搖由中國安也
此漢事之驗也
明興統御寰宇南盡海嵎北極沙漠日月所
出入咸就臣屬至我
皇上而德教所及天下景附響合魚鱗雜沓舉
踵內嚮思慕恐後夫既以際天地而
覆冒之矣間者物衆蕃孽島夷竊釁弄兵東南
===
乘軍吏之弗戒往往猖獗一時諸郡皆震
自羣臣相顧錯愕莫知計所出而我
皇上赫然斯怒易將命師
勅以廟略不旋踵而直犁賊巢縛其酋首斬
馘不可勝數東南用有成績而頃者西北
之寇挾持內逆重圍大同一日報數至內
有縣罄之憂外無强援之助此于勢尤急
而我
皇上亦一易置其間須臾而圍解賊逐雲中遂
