寸，駢首以就漢誅，由中國安也。陳豨兵精而起代，英布善陳而反楚，韓王信材武而連吳，諸侯數起而天下不搖，由中國安也。此漢事之驗也。
明興，統御寰宇，南盡海嵎，北極沙漠，日月所出入，咸就臣屬。至我皇上，而德教所及，天下景附響合，魚鱗雜沓，舉踵內嚮，思慕恐後。夫既以際天地而覆冒之矣。間者，物衆蕃孽，島夷竊釁，弄兵東南，乘軍吏之弗戒，往往猖獗，一時諸郡皆震。自羣臣相顧錯愕，莫知計所出，而我皇上赫然斯怒，易將命師，勅以廟略，不旋踵而直犁賊巢，縛其酋首，斬馘不可勝數。東南用有成績，而頃者西北之寇挾持內逆，重圍大同，一日報數至，內有縣罄之憂，外無强援之助，此于勢尤急。而我皇上亦一易置其間，須臾而圍解賊逐，雲中遂
translation_en:
…even an inch; they submitted together to execution by the Han because the central realm was secure. Chen Xi rose in Dai with elite troops; Ying Bu, skilled in battle formations, rebelled in Chu; and Xin, King of Han, a man of military talent and valor, allied himself with Wu [?]. The regional lords repeatedly rose in revolt, yet All Under Heaven remained unshaken because the central realm was secure. These events of the Han bear this out.
When the Ming arose, it united and governed the whole world, extending south to the shores of the sea and north to the deserts. Wherever the sun and moon rose and set, all submitted as subjects. Under our present Emperor, wherever his virtue and instruction reach, All Under Heaven follows like a shadow and responds like an echo. Crowding together like overlapping fish scales, they stand on tiptoe and turn toward the court, longing for him and fearing to fall behind. His sheltering care has indeed reached the utmost bounds of heaven and earth. Recently, as living things multiplied, malign growths arose [?]: the island barbarians seized an opening to wage war in the southeast. Taking advantage of the military officers’ lack of vigilance, they repeatedly ran rampant, and for a time all the prefectures were shaken. The assembled ministers looked at one another in consternation, unable to devise a plan. Our Emperor then blazed with anger, replaced the commanders, dispatched armies, and instructed them in the court’s strategy. In scarcely the time it takes to turn on one’s heel, they swept straight through the bandits’ lairs and bound their chieftains; the heads taken and ears cut off were beyond counting. Thus success was achieved in the southeast. More recently, however, raiders from the northwest, bringing internal rebels under their sway, laid close siege to Datong. Reports arrived several times a day. Within, there was fear of utter depletion; outside, no powerful reinforcements offered help. This situation was especially urgent. Yet our Emperor again made a single change of personnel there, and in a moment the siege was lifted and the bandits driven away. Yunzhong thereupon…

title: 嘉靖三十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
高枕而卧鼓腹而歌矣此惟我
皇上道合
玄化役使百靈故
意之所出而鬼神率從
命之所行而雷霆震盪其
神武駕馭有如此者然雲中則先飛輓以入餉
給牛種散錢以助耕東南則免民之租恤
民之苦其他遼海上谷諸地一以災
聞則立
===
賜往賑是蓋
皇上至仁聖德憯然惻怛之心非徒以捄一時
之敝然内安民生而外壯敵愾端寔在此
夫運籌策于尊爼而偃甲兵于四方脫百
姓之阽危躋一世于衽席固
大聖之事而帝王之宏軌也南北之醜又何足
以為泰山四維之間乎愚故曰非夷狄之
足患而在中國治安之有其具者蓋謂此
也然愚聞之君運于上而臣勞于下廟堂

高枕而卧，鼓腹而歌矣。此惟我皇上道合玄化，役使百靈，故意之所出而鬼神率從，命之所行而雷霆震盪，其神武駕馭有如此者。然雲中則先飛輓以入餉，給牛種、散錢以助耕；東南則免民之租，恤民之苦。其他遼海、上谷諸地，一以災聞，則立賜往賑。是蓋皇上至仁聖德，憯然惻怛之心，非徒以捄一時之敝，然内安民生而外壯敵愾，端寔在此。

夫運籌策于尊爼，而偃甲兵于四方，脫百姓之阽危，躋一世于衽席，固大聖之事，而帝王之宏軌也。南北之醜，又何足以為泰山四維之間乎？愚故曰，非夷狄之足患，而在中國治安之有其具者，蓋謂此也。

然愚聞之，君運于上而臣勞于下，廟堂
translation_en:
…rest with their pillows high and sing as they pat their well-fed bellies. This is solely because our Emperor’s Way accords with the mysterious workings of Heaven, and he commands the myriad spirits. Thus, wherever his intentions lead, the ghosts and spirits all follow; wherever his commands take effect, thunder shakes the world. Such is his divine martial power and mastery. Yet in Yunzhong he first expedited transport to bring in provisions, supplied cattle and seed, and distributed money to assist cultivation; in the southeast he remitted the people’s taxes and relieved their suffering. In other places, such as Liaohai and Shanggu, whenever a disaster was reported, he immediately bestowed aid to be taken there for relief. This surely manifests the Emperor’s utmost benevolence and sagely virtue, his deeply compassionate heart. It serves not merely to remedy the troubles of the moment: securing the people’s livelihood at home and strengthening their resolve against the enemy abroad truly depend upon this.

To devise strategies amid the ceremonial vessels of court and lay weapons to rest throughout the realm, to rescue the common people from imminent peril and bring an entire age into peaceful repose—these are indeed the accomplishments of a great sage and the grand pattern of emperors and kings. How could the vile foes of north and south possibly create a breach in the four bonds securing Mount Tai [?]? Thus, when I humbly say that the foreign peoples are not themselves sufficient cause for concern, but that the issue lies in whether the Central Kingdom possesses the means to secure order and peace, this is what I mean.

title: 嘉靖三十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
之臣贊于中而方鎮之臣成于外二者相
須自古而記之矣昔堯舜之時不獨二帝
之能安其民而當時亮采熈績之臣莫不
以二帝之心為心者故二帝得稱垂裳之
聖周之時不獨文武之能安其民而當時
篤棐保釐之臣莫不以文武之心為心者
故文武得稱盛王不獨宣王之能安其民
而當時出納藩翰之臣莫不以宣王之心
為心者故宣王得稱令主漢不足言矣而
===
其臣安定收集之功清净守成之道以及
夫長者之治皆能以其君之心為心者故
漢亦得以成四百之業今百官就列英賢
效用而天下稍稍有警則所在當事之臣
或至僨誤而令
廟堂數央其計
明主自親其文甚非所以代
上而安下也愚聞之事未至而防者豫也患未
形而圖者機也故曰土膏動者萌甲秋霜

punctuated:
之臣贊于中，而方鎮之臣成于外，二者相須，自古而記之矣。昔堯舜之時，不獨二帝之能安其民，而當時亮采熈績之臣，莫不以二帝之心為心者，故二帝得稱垂裳之聖。周之時，不獨文武之能安其民，而當時篤棐保釐之臣，莫不以文武之心為心者，故文武得稱盛王。不獨宣王之能安其民，而當時出納藩翰之臣，莫不以宣王之心為心者，故宣王得稱令主。漢不足言矣，而其臣安定收集之功、清净守成之道，以及夫長者之治，皆能以其君之心為心者，故漢亦得以成四百之業。
今百官就列，英賢效用，而天下稍稍有警，則所在當事之臣或至僨誤，而令廟堂數央其計，明主自親其文，甚非所以代上而安下也。愚聞之：事未至而防者，豫也；患未形而圖者，機也。故曰：土膏動者萌甲，秋霜
translation_en:
…the ministers at court assist within, while the ministers commanding the regions bring matters to completion outside. The two depend upon one another, as has been recorded since antiquity. In the time of Yao and Shun, it was not solely the abilities of the two emperors that brought peace to their people. The ministers of that age, who faithfully discharged their duties and advanced their achievements, all took the two emperors’ intentions as their own. Thus the two emperors could be acclaimed as sages who ruled with their robes hanging down, without exertion. In the Zhou era, it was not solely the abilities of Kings Wen and Wu that brought peace to their people. The ministers of that age, who steadfastly assisted them, protected the people, and administered affairs, all took Wen and Wu’s intentions as their own. Thus Wen and Wu could be acclaimed as illustrious kings. Nor was it solely King Xuan’s ability that brought peace to his people. The ministers of his age, who conveyed commands and counsel and served as bulwarks of the state, all took King Xuan’s intentions as their own. Thus King Xuan could be acclaimed as an excellent ruler. The Han scarcely merits discussion; nevertheless, its ministers’ achievements in pacifying the realm and gathering its scattered people, their practice of preserving the established order through quiet and unintrusive government, and their benevolent administration all reflected their ability to take their sovereign’s intentions as their own. Thus the Han too was able to establish its four-hundred-year dynastic enterprise.
Today the hundred officials occupy their appointed posts, and outstanding and worthy men devote their talents to service. Yet whenever even slight alarms arise in the realm, the officials responsible in the affected places sometimes mishandle affairs to the point of failure, causing the court repeatedly to seek plans [?] and the enlightened ruler personally to attend to the documents. This is very far from fulfilling their duty to act on behalf of the sovereign above and bring peace to the people below. I have heard that guarding against events before they arrive is preparedness, and devising measures against trouble before it takes shape is discernment of incipient change. Thus it is said: “When the fertile earth stirs, shoots break through their husks; when the autumn frost…”

title: 嘉靖三十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
降者木落言察機也晨炊者蘊火𤓰爁者
儲泉言貴豫也故弭冦者當弭于良民之
時而憂患者當憂于方治之日昨東南之
冦始發難于吳諸爲冦慮者皆在吳也既
而賊又轉鄞越矣則爲冦慮者皆在鄞越
也西北之冦始犯古北諸爲冦慮者皆在
古北也今而又犯雲中則爲冦慮者又皆
在雲中也其患賊常在其先而我應之反
隨其後彼先則不知所備我後則不知所
===
省不知所備則兵分不知所省則財費兵
分則詘財費則匱吾方慮其詘與匱而彼
又轉而他犯矣夫兵之所處荆棘生焉一
方有事三隅皆動今所以當賊者不特一
方也所以給備賊者不特三隅也夫人之
四肢百骸相列而分然肱病則惜肱手病
則愛足病于此則猶幸其免于彼今當事
諸臣忽而不省用財有事之方力竭無事
之地兵之所處而荆棘生其所不處而家

punctuated: 降者木落，言察機也；晨炊者蘊火，𤓰爁者儲泉，言貴豫也。故弭冦者當弭于良民之時，而憂患者當憂于方治之日。昨東南之冦始發難于吳，諸爲冦慮者皆在吳也；既而賊又轉鄞越矣，則爲冦慮者皆在鄞越也。西北之冦始犯古北，諸爲冦慮者皆在古北也；今而又犯雲中，則爲冦慮者又皆在雲中也。其患，賊常在其先，而我應之反隨其後。彼先則不知所備，我後則不知所省。不知所備則兵分，不知所省則財費；兵分則詘，財費則匱。吾方慮其詘與匱，而彼又轉而他犯矣。夫兵之所處，荆棘生焉。一方有事，三隅皆動。今所以當賊者，不特一方也；所以給備賊者，不特三隅也。夫人之四肢百骸，相列而分，然肱病則惜肱，手病則愛足，病于此則猶幸其免于彼。今當事諸臣忽而不省，用財有事之方，力竭無事之地。兵之所處而荆棘生，其所不處而家
translation_en:
…when frost descends, the trees shed their leaves: this speaks of discerning the first signs of change. Those who cook in the morning bank their fire; those concerned with burning [?] store up water: this speaks of valuing preparedness. Thus those who would quell banditry should do so while the people are still law-abiding, and those who would guard against calamity should be concerned while order still prevails.

Recently, when the bandits in the southeast first made trouble in Wu, all who concerned themselves with the bandit threat focused on Wu. Soon, however, the bandits shifted to Yin and Yue, and all who concerned themselves with the threat focused on Yin and Yue. When the raiders in the northwest first invaded Gubei, all who concerned themselves with the threat focused on Gubei. Now they have invaded Yunzhong, and all who concern themselves with the threat again focus on Yunzhong. The trouble is that the enemy always acts first, while our response follows behind. Because they act first, we do not know where to prepare defenses; because we lag behind, we do not know where to economize. Not knowing where to prepare defenses, we divide our forces; not knowing where to economize, we expend our funds. Divided forces become inadequate, and expended funds run short. While we are worrying over these inadequacies and shortages, the enemy shifts again and attacks elsewhere.

Where armies are stationed, thorns and brambles grow. When one region faces trouble, the other three quarters are all stirred into action. Now, more than a single region is engaged in confronting the enemy, and more than the other three quarters are supplying the preparations against them. A person's four limbs and many bones are arranged together yet distinct. When the upper arm is afflicted, one cherishes the upper arm; when the hand is afflicted, one protects the foot [?]. When illness strikes here, one still counts oneself fortunate that another part has escaped it. Now the officials responsible are heedless and fail to examine matters: funds are spent in the regions facing trouble, while resources are exhausted in the places free of trouble. Where armies are stationed, thorns and brambles grow; where they are not stationed, households…

title: 嘉靖三十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
室罄則是人之手足股肱相連而感不痛
者以病者而俱廢是自敝之道也古者受
君之命而撫綏斯民者其撫之而得則化
賊而爲良民反寇攘而爲治投戈釋劍而
歸農者即此民也其失則釀寇于治驅良
民而爲賊折竿棄耜而弄兵者亦即此民
也故安民所以息寇安中國所以禦夷狄
此古今不易之論也愚嘗考天下之勢有
可得而言者夫山東齊魯海岱之區畿邑
===
之東輔也内連燕趙習騎射喜椎埋而好
佛白蓮之徒因乘之操禍福之權以愚黔
首閭閻其所在而聚不可勝數歲如貍伏
應如蜂起不及今制之此五斗之遺患也
不可以不慮也河洛梁宋之郊四通八達
之地異日者潢池之戈方息而徒黨寔繁
今其巨寇往往而作或千金之家飽煖之
民而公爲盜首夫貧而爲盜常耳富而盜
者誠可愕也此不可以不慮也今天下無

punctuated:
室罄，則是人之手足股肱相連而感，不痛者以病者而俱廢，是自敝之道也。古者受君之命而撫綏斯民者，其撫之而得，則化賊而爲良民，反寇攘而爲治，投戈釋劍而歸農者，即此民也；其失，則釀寇于治，驅良民而爲賊，折竿棄耜而弄兵者，亦即此民也。故安民所以息寇，安中國所以禦夷狄，此古今不易之論也。
愚嘗考天下之勢，有可得而言者。夫山東齊魯海岱之區，畿邑之東輔也。内連燕趙，習騎射，喜椎埋而好佛。白蓮之徒因乘之，操禍福之權以愚黔首，閭閻其所在而聚，不可勝數。歲如貍伏，應如蜂起。不及今制之，此五斗之遺患也，不可以不慮也。河洛梁宋之郊，四通八達之地，異日者潢池之戈方息，而徒黨寔繁。今其巨寇往往而作，或千金之家、飽煖之民，而公爲盜首。夫貧而爲盜，常耳；富而盜者，誠可愕也。此不可以不慮也。今天下無
translation_en:
…households are emptied of their resources. This is like a person's hands, feet, thighs, and arms, all connected and affecting one another: even those that do not hurt become incapacitated along with those that are diseased. This is the way to exhaust oneself. In antiquity, those who received their ruler's command to pacify and care for the people, if successful in doing so, transformed bandits into law-abiding subjects and turned pillage into good order. Those who laid down their spears, relinquished their swords, and returned to farming were these very people. If such officials failed, however, they bred banditry amid good order and drove law-abiding subjects to become bandits. Those who broke off poles for weapons, abandoned their ploughs, and took up arms were also these very people. Thus, bringing peace to the people is the means to end banditry; bringing peace to the Central Realm is the means to repel the barbarians. This principle has remained unchanged from antiquity to the present.
I have humbly examined conditions throughout the realm and have some observations to offer. Shandong, the region of Qi and Lu, the sea and Mount Dai, forms the eastern bulwark of the capital region. Inland it adjoins Yan and Zhao. Its people practice mounted archery, have a taste for murder and clandestine burial, and are devoted to Buddhism. Followers of the White Lotus exploit this, wielding supposed power over misfortune and blessing to delude the common people. They gather wherever they are found among the villages and neighborhoods, in numbers beyond counting. For years they lurk like wildcats [?]; when called upon, they rise like a swarm of bees. Unless they are brought under control now, this will be a lingering scourge of the kind left by the Five Pecks of Rice movement. This cannot be ignored.
The districts of He, Luo, Liang, and Song are a crossroads accessible from every direction. The recent petty rebellion had only just subsided, yet its adherents remained numerous. Now major bandits repeatedly arise there. Some come from households worth a thousand pieces of gold, people well fed and warmly clothed, yet openly become bandit leaders. That the poor turn to banditry is commonplace; that the wealthy become bandits is truly alarming. This cannot be ignored. At present, those parts of the realm without …

title: 嘉靖三十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
事獨江右諸郡爲全而湖廣自苗叛之後
稍息肩者數年然近者賊自贛入將薄豫
章以及全楚雖幸撲滅而諸郡亦頗動矣
夫江右地險而民貧險則賊易以阻民貧
則不能以支賊是固所當先備者而全楚
江漢沮澤之場萑蒲之藪是干櫓之窟而
嘯聚之巢也此不可以不慮也凡愚之說
其地則中國之要樞而事則審機防豫之
當先者也防之于豫則一方之事坐失其
===
機則天下之憂惟一方之臣失其防而後
天下以爲患自往者皆然故愚以爲當事
者之責也

事獨江右諸郡爲全而湖廣自苗叛之後
稍息有者數年然近者賊自贛入將薄豫
章以及全楚雖幸樸滅而諸郡亦頗動矣

當先者也防之于豫則一方之事坐失其
===
機則天下之憂惟一方之臣失其防而後
天下以爲患自往者皆然故愚以爲當事
者之責也
punctuated: 事，獨江右諸郡爲全，而湖廣自苗叛之後，稍息肩者數年。然近者賊自贛入，將薄豫章以及全楚，雖幸撲滅，而諸郡亦頗動矣。夫江右地險而民貧，險則賊易以阻，民貧則不能以支賊，是固所當先備者。而全楚，江漢沮澤之場，萑蒲之藪，是干櫓之窟而嘯聚之巢也，此不可以不慮也。凡愚之說，其地則中國之要樞，而事則審機防豫之當先者也。防之于豫，則一方之事；坐失其機，則天下之憂。惟一方之臣失其防，而後天下以爲患，自往者皆然。故愚以爲當事者之責也。
translation_en:
…is at peace. Only the prefectures of Jiangyou remain intact, while Huguang has enjoyed a few years of respite since the Miao rebellion. Recently, however, bandits entered from Gan, threatening to advance upon Yuzhang and reach the whole of Chu. Although they were fortunately wiped out, the prefectures were nevertheless considerably shaken. Jiangyou has rugged terrain and an impoverished population. Rugged terrain makes it easy for bandits to entrench themselves; poverty leaves the people unable to withstand them. This is certainly a region where preparations should take priority. As for the whole of Chu, its marshlands along the Jiang and Han rivers and its thickets of reeds and rushes provide lairs for armed men and nests where outlaws gather. This cannot be left out of consideration.

In all that I have humbly discussed, the places concerned are crucial strategic centers of the realm, and the matters concerned demand priority in assessing incipient dangers and taking precautions. If precautions are taken in advance, the affair concerns only one region; if the opportunity is allowed to slip away, it becomes a source of anxiety for all under Heaven. Only after the officials of one region have failed to maintain their defenses does the trouble become a calamity for the whole realm. It has always been so in the past. Thus, in my humble judgment, responsibility rests with those in charge.

translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination

In the wuwu year of Jiajing [1558], Shuntian Prefecture was again due to hold the Provincial Examination. His Majesty commanded your servants Fen and Gong to go and preside over it. Once the record was completed, it fell to your servant Gong to write its postface.

Your servant reflects that Yao and Shun established their capitals at Pingban [?], and many of their sagely and wise assistants came from Ji; Kings Wen and Wu dwelt at Feng and Hao, and many of the outstanding talents of their age were born in Yong. Why was this? Although the rising sun shines everywhere throughout the myriad regions, Yanggu and Xianchi receive its light first, and thus feel its influence especially deeply. Yet the transforming work of Heaven and Earth reaches fulfillment through enduring constancy. Unless governance extends over many years, allowing its nurturing influence to penetrate thoroughly, how could it foster outstanding and worthy men who emerge generation after generation without exhaustion? Thus Yao lived for 118 years, Shun for 110 years, King Wen for 97 years, and King Wu for…

title: 嘉靖三十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
九十有三年其德衍而靡窮
其意悠而不迫是以太和之
氣萃於人文岳牧盈庭而宅
俊列席者也夫豈一朝一夕
致然哉仰惟我
皇上天縱神聖撫運中興以
道德養蒸黎以
===
禮樂陶萬國漸摩淪浹三十七
年於茲方將配
天地之無疆同
大明之久照有不止如堯舜文武
焉者至順所積即翔泳之物
罔弗歸德而况於人乎况於
士乎况於在都邑者乎固宜

translation_en:
…ninety-three years. Their virtue spread without limit; their intentions were far-reaching and unhurried. Thus the vital energy of supreme harmony gathered in human culture: chief ministers and regional governors filled their courts, and eminent men were established in their seats. How could this have come about in a single morning or evening?
Looking reverently upward, we reflect that our Emperor, endowed by Heaven with divine sagacity, has responded to the course of destiny and brought about a restoration. Through the Way and virtue he nurtures the common people; through ritual and music he molds the myriad states. This gradual cultivation and thorough permeation have now continued for thirty-seven years. He is about to match Heaven and Earth in their boundlessness and equal the sun in its enduring illumination, going beyond even Yao, Shun, King Wen, and King Wu. Where perfect harmony has accumulated, even creatures that fly and swim all turn toward his virtue. How much more, then, human beings! How much more scholars! How much more those in the capital! Surely it is fitting that…

title: 嘉靖三十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
有英賢輩出如昔之冀與雍
者以為
國之楨率先天下用之而弗匱
者也乃臣今得縱閱其文往
往據理要切事情論治則祖
唐虞論道則師周孔論志則
尊義而賤利論人則好正而
===
嫉邪卓犖雄渾之氣勃如溢
如莫可抑遏以是想見其人
即古人何讓焉臣則竊慶嘆
曰文盛矣哉自非
聖人在上涵育有年何能至是乃
益信作人由諸壽考詩人所
稱非虛也然臣於此復有餘
alt_text:
有英賢輩出如昔之冀與雍
者以爲
國之楨率先天下用之而弗匱
者也乃臣令得縱閱其文往
往據理要切事情論治則祖
唐虞論道則師周孔論志則
尊義而賤利論人則好正而
===
嫉邪卓犖雄渾之氣勃如溢
如莫可抑遏以是想見其人
即古人何讓焉臣則竊慶嘆
曰文盛矣哉自非
聖人在上涵育有年何能至是乃
益信作人由諸壽考詩人所
稱非虛也然臣於此復有餘
punctuated: 有英賢輩出，如昔之冀與雍者，以為國之楨，率先天下，用之而弗匱者也。乃臣今得縱閱其文，往往據理，要切事情。論治則祖唐虞，論道則師周孔，論志則尊義而賤利，論人則好正而嫉邪。卓犖雄渾之氣，勃如溢如，莫可抑遏。以是想見其人，即古人何讓焉！臣則竊慶嘆曰：「文盛矣哉！自非聖人在上，涵育有年，何能至是？」乃益信作人由諸壽考，詩人所稱非虛也。然臣於此復有餘
translation_en:
…outstanding and worthy men should emerge in succession, as they once did in Ji and Yong, to serve as pillars of the state, lead all under Heaven, and provide an inexhaustible supply of talent for service. Now that I, your servant, have been able to read their writings at length, I find that they frequently ground their arguments in principle and address the realities of affairs with precision. In discussing government, they take the reigns of Yao and Shun as their model; in discussing the Way, they follow the Duke of Zhou and Confucius as their teachers; in discussing aspirations, they esteem righteousness and disdain profit; in judging men, they favor the upright and detest the depraved. An extraordinary, powerful, and full-bodied spirit surges and overflows, impossible to restrain. From these writings one can envision the men themselves: in what respect need they yield even to the ancients?
I therefore privately rejoice and exclaim: “How flourishing is literary accomplishment! Had the sage sovereign not been on high, nurturing them over many years, how could it have reached this point?” I am thus all the more convinced that the cultivation of men proceeds from the sovereign’s long life, and that what the poet praised was no empty claim. Yet in this I still have further…

title: 嘉靖三十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
懼焉何者昔堯舜時雖敷奏
用言然必試功而後庸文武
之法有言揚者矣亦必任事
而後禄豈非以言取人即盛
世有未敢必者哉則臣於今
日又安敢必謂盡得人也兹
役也臣寔夙夜惴惴焉殫厥
===
心惟其言平正通達是取厥
或鉤棘為竒浮夸為博閃爍
而無當游揚而不情諸若此
者即華采烜爛如綺如繡直
黜之不復顧惜何也
國家取士非為言也將緣是以
覘知其為人也即皆平正通

而後祿豈非以言取人即盛
世有未敢必者哉則臣於今
日又安敢必謂盡得人也茲
役也臣寔夙夜惴惴焉殫厥
心惟其言平正通達是取厥
===
或鈎棘爲奇浮夸爲博閃爍
而無當游揚而不情諸若此
者即華采烜爛如綺如繡直
黜之不復顧惜何也
國家取士非爲言也將緣是以
覘知其爲人也即皆平正通
punctuated: 懼焉。何者？昔堯舜時，雖敷奏用言，然必試功而後庸；文武之法，有言揚者矣，亦必任事而後禄。豈非以言取人，即盛世有未敢必者哉？則臣於今日，又安敢必謂盡得人也？兹役也，臣寔夙夜惴惴焉，殫厥心，惟其言平正通達是取。厥或鉤棘為竒，浮夸為博，閃爍而無當，游揚而不情，諸若此者，即華采烜爛，如綺如繡，直黜之，不復顧惜。何也？國家取士，非為言也，將緣是以覘知其為人也。即皆平正通
translation_en: …apprehension remains. Why is this? In the days of Yao and Shun, although men were heard presenting their statements and their words were accepted, they were employed only after their achievements had been tested. Under the institutions of Kings Wen and Wu, some were advanced on the strength of their words, yet they too received emoluments only after being entrusted with duties. Does this not show that even in an age of flourishing government, selecting men by their words was something whose reliability one dared not take for granted? How, then, could your servant now dare assert with certainty that all those selected are worthy men? In this assignment, your servant has indeed been anxious morning and night, exerting his utmost care and selecting only those whose writing is balanced, upright, clear, and coherent. As for those who take tangled obscurity for originality and empty exaggeration for breadth of learning, whose words are evasive and without substance, or expansive and untrue to reality—all such writings I reject outright without further regret, even if their brilliant ornament shines like patterned silk or embroidery. Why? The state selects scholars not for their words alone, but to discern through these what sort of men they are. Even if all their writing is balanced, upright, and clear…

title: 嘉靖三十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
達如所取者且所覘或未可
諒乃其言即爾爾斯其人已
可識矣而又何覘焉臣竊觀
時俗率好以虛辭爲業不遡
本始以儇利爲才不右質直
以形迹爲行誼不崇心術以
文飾爲事功不求真實允若
===
時即所自處亦既欺甚矣尚
敢望其身致誠信奉
主上之役使哉故臣於覘知之際
其去取乃如此也於戲主司
之心至是則竭矣無復能爲
者矣繼自今務自樹立以逭
主司不明之罪者在爾多士

本始以儇利爲才不右質直
以形迹爲行誼不崇心術以
文飾爲事功不求真實允若
===
時即所旨處亦既欺甚矣尚
敢望其身致誠信奉
主上之使使哉故臣於覘知之際
其去取乃如此也於戲主司
之心至是則竭矣無復能爲
者矣繼自今務自樹立以追
主司不明之罪者在爾多士
punctuated:
達如所取者，且所覘或未可諒；乃其言即爾爾，斯其人已可識矣，而又何覘焉？臣竊觀時俗，率好以虛辭爲業，不遡本始；以儇利爲才，不右質直；以形迹爲行誼，不崇心術；以文飾爲事功，不求真實。允若時，即所自處亦既欺甚矣，尚敢望其身致誠信，奉主上之役使哉？故臣於覘知之際，其去取乃如此也。
於戲！主司之心至是則竭矣，無復能爲者矣。繼自今，務自樹立，以逭主司不明之罪者，在爾多士。
translation_en:
…lucid, like the writings we select, what we discern of their authors may still not be reliable. But if their words are merely of that other sort, their character is already apparent: what further scrutiny is needed? Your servant observes that prevailing custom generally favors making empty phrases one’s occupation, without tracing things to their foundations; treating glib cleverness as talent, without esteeming straightforward integrity; treating outward appearances as virtuous conduct, without honoring the dispositions of the heart; and treating ornamental display as achievement, without seeking substance and truth. If this is indeed so, their conduct toward themselves is already profoundly deceptive. How could one still dare hope that they would personally attain sincerity and trustworthiness and serve at Your Majesty’s command? Thus, when scrutinizing candidates to understand their character, your servant has accepted and rejected them in this manner.
Alas! At this point the chief examiner has exhausted his care; there is nothing further he can do. From now on, it rests with you, the assembled candidates, to strive to establish yourselves, thereby sparing the chief examiner the blame for a lack of discernment.

title: 嘉靖三十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
詩曰彼都人士出言有章行
歸於周萬民所望夫都士之
爲民望也者豈惟其出言有
章爾哉固以行之周也爾多
士誠自樹立致誠信以奉役
使則固可以爲
國之楨率先天下允哉萬民之
===
望也已不然而徒以其言止
焉非所敢知也詩曰我不見
兮我心不說將無有嘆息而
譏者乎乃於
天地久成之化
大明首被之光不既自棄自背矣
乎其爲都士也則何貴矣不

乎其爲都士也則何貴矣不
punctuated: 詩曰：「彼都人士，出言有章，行歸於周，萬民所望。」夫都士之爲民望也者，豈惟其出言有章爾哉？固以行之周也。爾多士誠自樹立，致誠信以奉役使，則固可以爲國之楨，率先天下，允哉萬民之望也已！不然而徒以其言止焉，非所敢知也。詩曰：「我不見兮，我心不說。」將無有嘆息而譏者乎？乃於天地久成之化、大明首被之光，不既自棄自背矣乎？其爲都士也，則何貴矣？不
translation_en: The Book of Poetry says: “Those men of the capital—their speech has elegance; they return to Zhou, and all the people look up to them.” Is it merely because their speech has elegance that the people look up to the capital’s scholars? Surely it is because their conduct is well-rounded. If you scholars truly establish yourselves and bring sincerity and trustworthiness to the service entrusted to you, you can indeed become pillars of the state and take the lead throughout the realm. Truly, you will fulfill the hopes of all the people! If, however, you go no further than words alone, I dare not presume to know what will become of you. The Book of Poetry says: “I do not see them; my heart is not glad.” Will there not be those who sigh and reproach you? Would you not then have abandoned and betrayed the transforming influence long nurtured by Heaven and Earth, and the radiance of the Great Ming bestowed first upon you? What value would there be in your being scholars of the capital? Not …

title: 嘉靖三十七年順天府鄉試錄
text:
寧是也臣聞鳳之性仁其出
也為瑞而天下治鳥有曰昭
明者五色而象鳳其性不仁
而出則天下多事臣今之必
以平正通達取士也誠見其
五色謂為鳳也脫不幸而有
昭明者焉出乎其間則
===
國事或為之蠹詎惟科目羞乎
此臣所為重懼於多士之進
惓惓規飭而不容已者也嗟
爾多士其必思所以無負
今日也哉
翰林院侍讀高拱謹序
alt_text:
寍是也臣聞鳳之性仁其出
也爲瑞而天下治鳥有日昭
明者五色而象鳳其性不仁
而出則天下多事臣今之必
以平正通達取士也誠見其
五色謂爲鳳也脫不幸而有
昭明者爲出乎其間則
===
國事彧爲之蠹詎惟科目羞乎
此臣所爲重懼於多士之進
惓惓規飭而不容已者也嗟
爾多士其必思所以無負
今日也哉
翰林院侍讀高拱謹序
punctuated:
寧是也。臣聞鳳之性仁，其出也為瑞，而天下治。鳥有曰昭明者，五色而象鳳，其性不仁，而出則天下多事。臣今之必以平正通達取士也，誠見其五色，謂為鳳也。脫不幸而有昭明者焉，出乎其間，則國事或為之蠹，詎惟科目羞乎？此臣所為重懼於多士之進，惓惓規飭而不容已者也。嗟爾多士，其必思所以無負今日也哉！
翰林院侍讀高拱謹序。
translation_en:
…only this. Your servant has heard that the phoenix is benevolent by nature: its appearance is an auspicious sign, and the realm is well governed. There is a bird called the Zhaoming, whose five-colored plumage resembles the phoenix’s. Its nature, however, is not benevolent, and when it appears, the realm is beset by troubles. Your servant’s insistence today on selecting men of fairness, uprightness, and comprehensive understanding is indeed like seeing their five-colored plumage and judging them to be phoenixes. Should a Zhaoming unfortunately emerge among them, affairs of state might suffer its depredations. Would this merely bring disgrace upon the examinations? This is why your servant feels such profound apprehension about the advancement of the many scholars, and cannot cease earnestly admonishing and exhorting them. Ah, you scholars, you must surely consider how to prove yourselves worthy of this day!
Preface respectfully composed by Gao Gong, Reader-in-Waiting of the Hanlin Academy.
